body: Due to our tour of Sri Lanka, our guide also offered us a private safari tour with 100% elephant sighting guarantee.So we changed from our bus to an off-road vehicle.We saw 4 herds of elephants with a total of about 50 - 60 animals during our 2-1/2 hour tour of the Hurulu Eco Park. That was really great!However, we were very! divided as to the peace of the animals. Clearly, the drivers discuss where a herd of elephants is right now, but then there's no stopping them. At the entrance of the park there are signs saying that drivers should not approach the elephants more than 50 meters. Nobody cares about that there. As soon as a herd is sighted, the paths are left and partly driven to within 40 cm! of the thick skins 😡.Once we could even observe that the herd, except for a small passage, was literally encircled.On the one hand you should think about the animals that have no rest at all during the day and on the other hand, what if such an animal becomes aggressive? The vehicles are so tightly packed together that it would be impossible to think of driving away quickly. That's where total panic would break out.Very, very sad that the people actually responsible here are acting so irresponsibly
title: More urgent thought needs to be given to elephants

body: We took part in an afternoon safari in the park. We saw a lot of elephants, both big and cubs. At the end of the tour we walked up a rock with panoramic views. Nice experience, not comparable to a safari in Africa, but still nice.
title: Lots of elephants

body: A great afternoon with a good driver and a very competent guide
title: We really enjoyed doing this safari with a driver and a high quality guide. We have been able to admire

body: Superb park , we saw about thirty elephants sometimes with family with young or alone. The elephants seem happy because in total freedom and only 25% of the park is accessible to tourists.
title: Great experience

body: The driver did a good job. We were picked up by jeep and paid 12,000Lkr and the entrance on site (we + jeep) 5000Lkr. We paid everything in Lkr as in $ this was much more expensive booked this through our stay. We took a 1/2 day tour which was more than sufficient. In total we saw about 40 elephants. We would do this again this way
title: 1/2 day elephant watching

body: We went to Hurulu Eco Park hoping to see elephants in the wild. We were lucky enough to spot several. However, I don’t feel good after witnessing these….. Whenever the elephants are spotted, many jeeps would move towards the location and gather around the area. The jeeps would get very close to the elephants. Many of the drivers would keep their engine on. The tourists would make exciting noise. It was quite chaotic.There were occasions where the elephants looked confused and didn’t know whether they should cross the road because of the presence of many jeeps. There was no space to cross the road. This made me feel super uncomfortable.I know that the safaris are an essential part of the tourism industry in Sri Lanka. Everyone is excited to visit elephants safaris. However, I wish there are stricter rules like turning off engines, minimizing noise, jeeps not getting too close, etc.These are wild animals, and they deserve to move freely and peacefully in their own home.I am grateful I saw them but I hope future visits can be done in a way that puts the elephants’ wellbeing first.
title: Amazing to see elephants closed up but the experience left me uneasy

body: Great experience with environmentally aware driver. This is a very busy area but our driver managed to find us some quiet places where we got some great photos. Close enough to hear the Elephants breathing.
title: Great Experience

body: Terrible experience. Basically, imagine a traffic jam of 60 4x4 jeeps lined up on a dirt road. We breathed exhaust gases for 3 hours, not being able to see much because of traffic. Terrible experience and not to do and especially not to recommend if you like nature! You don't have to subsidize experiences like that.This is not a safari. The average tourist target was also very low (people throwing cigarette butts) and drivers incited to throw pineapple residue from the jeep to attract elephants
title: Traffic jam in 4x4 without seeing anything. REAL SCAM, not a SAFARI

body: This is a beautiful national park, but the way elephant sightings are handled is extremely upsetting. Within just five minutes of entering the park, we counted around 50 jeeps surrounding only five elephants, effectively trapping them and completely ignoring their need for space. The elephants visibly looked disturbed, and it was heartbreaking to witness.There are clearly no enforced rules on how many vehicles can crowd wildlife, which turns what should be a respectful safari experience into chaos. Wildlife tourism should never come at the expense of the animals’ wellbeing.After we explained to our driver that we wanted to observe elephants from a distance and in their natural habitat, he did an excellent job. He took us away from the crowds, kept a respectful distance, and allowed us to enjoy watching the elephants calmly. This showed that a better experience is possible—if drivers and the park choose to prioritise it.Until stricter regulations are put in place to protect the animals, it’s hard to recommend this park despite its natural beauty.
title: Disappointing wildlife management despite a beautiful park

body: Organized through our hotel Tantor Resort we were picked up at the hotel at 7am. Cost for driver 8000 RS and entrance 5000 RS. Duration approx. 3.5 h. Although there have been several jeeps on the road, it spreads well. At the entrance, monkeys were waiting for inattentive tourists to steal their food. It worked, too. Jumped right into the jeep. We probably saw about 20 elephants in different groups, our driver drove very close so the animals were up to 2 m away from us. They didn't seem to mind us. In addition, many birds and even a crocodile could be observed. The ride in the jeep is rough, you just have to hold on well. It was a beautiful experience.
title: Be sure to join

body: A place to see animals in the wild, not tied up / chained for public rides and humiliation, families of Elephants, wild birds, snakes lizards all living in their natural surroundings, yes viewed by the public , but mostly just ignoring them and meandering where they want and eating as they go. A better place to see animals than in captivity. Post the tour enjoy a sundowner cocktail ( very refreshing )
title: see animals in the wild, not in captivity.

body: We had done a private tour during our stay in sigiriyaWhat an experience this Safari What a huge eco park where so much beauty can be seen.We enjoyed this day Can anyone recommend this safari
title: What an experience!!!

body: Amazing trip. Thank you, Hansika, at Lakpura. Would recommend this to any tourist and anyone visiting Sri Lanka who hasn’t seen Elephants up close!
title: Amazing experience and super time.

body: Amazing and unforgettable experience! 🌿🐘During today’s safari in Sri Lanka we saw a lot of elephants, very close and in full respect of their natural habitat – truly emotional and breathtaking.The guide was excellent: very knowledgeable, kind and attentive, explaining everything with passion and making the safari even more special.The company Hurulu Eco Park Private Safari was absolutely professional, with perfect organization and great respect for nature and wildlife.A truly authentic and memorable experience. Highly recommended to anyone visiting Sri Lanka!
title: Super Safari

body: Nature and animals is 5 stars.3 stars is because there are other park in the area that have better reviews. It was raining and we saw a few elephants and that was it.We felt is over rated and there is more hype and reality.
title: Good Park but over rated for sure

body: We had a fantastic time on the Safari. Our driver, Mayura, was constantly looking for the elephants and predicting where they would move to next.This mean we have some incredible 'close encounters' with the elephants whilst they wanderers around eating in the vegetation.
title: Got so much close than we expected!

body: Safari really fantastic. We have seen many elephants without disturbing them. The guide was really respectful and really very interesting. He showed us birds and small animals. Elephants are quiet and especially are neither with a chain nor with picks on the body. Of course, you can't touch them but that's normal. Elephants look very happy. I recommend without hesitation.
title: Beautiful elephants

body: We saw no wild life other than two groups of elephants, These were one group of three and another of five. The first group was surrounded by 20 jeeps, the second by such a large number of jeeps that I could not count them.In fact the most interesting aspect of the “safari” was watching the jeeps tussle for position round the poor elephants, with no regard for the elephants. But a long way to come and a high price to pay to watch jeepsIn our two hours in the jeep we saw nothing else of interestSo save your money was pass on the “attraction”
title: Do not bother, you will see more jeeps than elephants

body: Great Experiences. Just last minute decided to visit , but my husband was not interested to Jungle safari. We have stayed at Amaya Lake , Dambulla . So I enjoyed the solo Jeep safari at the evening. Enjoyed the stunning sunset also.
title: Solo safari

body: No regard or respect for the beautiful wild elephants. Too many jeeps surrounding them and one even got between mother and baby the mother then went to attack our keep as a warning to stay away and ripped the side rain cover from the jeep. Had a much better experience at yala where driver have to stick to the road
title: Too many jeeps surrounding the elephants

body: Great experience and great first for us. We have seen a good forty elephants, babies with their mothers, males, but also various birds, trees and flowers. At the 1st herd seen, there were about 10 cars and then it dispersed on various paths.
title: Amazing.

body: We had a privately hired tracker/guide who was truly excellent, he spotted several groups of elephants. However, within minutes large numbers of jeeps roared up and parked without any concern for the animals. Many of them seemed totally unconcerned that they were causing the elephants distrees. And the tourists within them were just as bad, most of them seemed just concerned to get a selfie, not really interested in the animals at all. Jeeps blocked the track of the elephants (we were in quite dense bush) and even parked in the muddy pool the elephants wanted to use to cool themselves down. There were lots of small elephants and older females protecting them and one of the biggest charged one of the jeeps that was too close. It was appalling.
title: Dreadful behaviour of the jeeps

body: We were very happy that the team informed us in advance about elephants moving out of minaraya reserve and advised us to go to nearby eco resort to watch elephants and it was such a good advice as we managed to see many elephants including the rare male tusker elephant. Very professional and well managed safari. I will recommend to all my friends
title: Super experience! Very well organized

body: Hi All!! I'm a tour guide in Sri Lanka so i did wild elephants watching safari on Hurulu eco park since 2010, it was a amazing experience i saw more than 30 elephants all times that I went there that's a minim - usually we have more then 7,000 elephants in that aria. so I would like to highly recommend this place for all tourists thanks
title: best experience ever in my life

body: If you visited Yala before, don’t waste time nor money to visit Hurulo Eco Park: has very little fauna diversity but, above all, drivers/guides are completely disrespectful of the nature. After we spotted a herd of 6 elephants, suddenly it was surrounded by 15 vehicles, off track into the bush, getting close to the animals with complete disregard for the herd. After we saw vehicles stopped with people out of the vehicle. And our driver even asked if we wanted him to grab a snake. This is not a natural park. If the park authorities, tourism operators and drivers don’t uphold the values to support and preserve wildlife, then it will be a matter of time until they’re out of job…and Sri Lanka poorer in biodiversity and nature
title: Sri Lanka trip

body: We felt like we were on a drive-hunt. They've seen some elephants. Where we then saw elephants with a baby elephant, more and more jeeps came racing and pushed the animals, was enough for us. The animals then ran back and forth in a bit of a panic and the jeeps continued to follow. We dropped out then!
title: Treibjagd?

body: An experience that will remain etched in our memories is certain! We met many elephants, single males and groups of females, babies including one who had just been born. The experience was magical, we are reassured to see that the driver leaves enough space around the animals.Only downside, a lot of Jeep (of which we are part) as soon as there is a grouping of elephants, not all are as attentive to the respect of the space of animals (they get very close and this can create a traffic jam. Not sure the animals like it).My advice: choose an experienced guide. Ours made us take small paths and we quickly separated from the other Jeep, which was very nice. The sunset was beautiful and we could still observe the elephants quietly.
title: Elephants everywhere

body: We have been on Safari in a game park in South Africa and this was quite different. In SA there would only ever be two jeeps at any one site at a time. Here, whenever an elephant appears there will be 10+ vehicles jockeying for position to get the best view. That takes the edge off it a bit however it’s still a great experience. We got to see several elephants up close. Even with all the vehicles the animals were never surrounded, so they could head back into the bush if they had been disturbed by the attention. They didn’t appear upset at all.So it’s not the Serengeti but worth doing nonetheless.
title: A bit crowded but still good

body: Great safari, incredible pictures and very close to the elephants and familyGreat and unforgettable pictures ! Always happy and fully recommended if you are in Sri Lanka.
title: Elephant safari with great guide Dammika; constantly the roof open and closed again in rain showers

body: We were there with a guide who was arranged directly by the accommodation (Atea Resort)! That was a stroke of luck! He drove very attentively through the park and spotted elephants where other guides passed by. In total we certainly saw 20 elephants in the 3h, including a few baby elephants! Was a super nice tour of the park! Recommendation: Take LOTS of water with you when it's hot!
title: beautiful park with many elephants

body: More elephants can be seen there without travelling much. Nice and quiet park in Sri Lanka near to the Lion Rock in Sigiriya. Hope you visit soon.
title: Elephants Safari.

body: We chose the Hurulu Ecopark safari with pickup at Sigiriya. The driver came on time, gave us all a chilled water bottle, took care of the tickets, and drove us around the reserve. It was slow going at first, but eventually we were able to see wild elephants. Our driver did his best to explain to us a bit about Elephants with his limited English, we appreciated his effort. We tried to get a Naturalist for the booking, but getting one depends on availability. We're grateful to have seen so many elephants, including a super close up of a baby when we were driving back to our hotel. Just know it can get really hot, so bring sunscreen, a hat, sun glasses, and wear comfortable clothes. The vehicle we were in was modern and clean.
title: If You Want to See Wild Sri Lankan Elephants

body: Great park to get very close to elephants in the wild, had half day safari with the company in the photo, think $55 per person, so worth it, informative safe driver,got very close to many groups of elephants and also saw lots of other interesting birds and wildlife. Much better than seeing then chained in the orphanage for the tourists pleasure.

body: The landscapes are beautiful! We saw a lot of elephants. The guide was very friendly and was able to answer all our questions. That is undoubtedly the reservation to be made. Tip: in the morning it is all the more beautiful!
title: Great experience!

body: Great place to see elephants and enjoy the wild life. We have seen many elephants with kids plus there is a great spot to see the park from the rock.

title: Lack of respect for animals by aggresive safari van drivers

title: Many beautiful elephants

body: In general, we had some luck and saw elephants there, so we had a nice experience. However, not much of any other wildlife is there. title: Okayish experience but not stunned

body: Cute but not exciting park with elephant spotting (and little else). Too many Jeeps and too high the cost for what you see.
title: Not satisfactory

body: Our family trip to Habarana was amazing, especially with our visit to Hurulu Eco Park to see wild elephants. For an unforgettable experience, head to Hurulu Eco Park from December to January. This park provides a unique opportunity to see elephants in their natural habitat as they complete their migration. The serene landscapes and diverse wildlife make Hurulu Eco Park a standout destination for nature lovers and wildlife enthusiasts.
title: Unforgettable Elephant Migration Experience at Hurulu Eco Park

body: Noticed a number of posts commenting about not being able to get up close to see the elephant... i've had a blast mine was a small jeep we could get into the bushes easily, yes the road conditions are rough but it's a park i don't expect a flat road anyway. i saw at least 30+ elephants and at least 10 of them up close like within reach. It was amazing.
title: Find a small jeep and you will enjoy your time!

body: We have enjoyed nature so much, those impressive pachyderms, we wanted to take one with us... Too bad they don't fit in the suitcase.... title: Good for elephant watching
