Fortunately there were relatively few visitors and therefore traffic in the park.
title: Great experience, wonderful trip!

body: You can see the elephant even in day time. I booked my jeep at 10.15 am and still we were lucky to see the elephants. The nature was so beautiful. Roads are better than yala park.
title: Day time tour.

body: This park is the closest of the 3 located around Habarana. Elephants migrate from one park to another too, so find out which one is best to visit. Don't expect to see any animals other than elephants. There are a lot of jeeps full of tourists (we are one of them!) so they all converge in the same place as soon as a family of elephants is spotted.
title: Traffic jams on the slopes!

body: I was really looking forward to the Jeep safari in search of the Elephants but due to the very heavy rains recently the tracks through this park have been severely damaged and are barely passable in places, so the three hour journey was like being thrown around in a washing machine. In addition on the afternoon I went there were just too many Jeeps chasing the same groups of Elephants and unless you were at the front of the convoy when they stopped you were too far back to see much action and it was like being stuck in a traffic jam of jeeps all jostling to get a better position. Out of the 3 hours we managed about 10 minutes of close proximity to these wonderful creatures and the rest of the time it was just not enjoyable, which was a real shame.
title: Terribly overcrowded Elephant safari on horrendous roads

body: Maybe due to the weather, but today the park was really overcrowded: rows of jeeps lined up along the same path, sometimes trying to overtake them to get to a possible sighting of elephants before the others (the only animal that lives in the park, I think: apart from two eagles, we saw nothing else). When elephants were spotted, the jeeps lined up in double rows to let as many people see them; often, leaving the engine running to be able to "sprint" when some car in a good position moved to continue. We saw several elephants, but with all those people, it felt more like a zoo than a park. I don't recommend it.
title: Too crowded

body: I was taken for a jeep tour in the morning to Hurulu eco park. It was a great experience. We saw lots of elephants at least over twenty. Since it was early there were only 4-5 jeeps in the park so it was fairly quiet. The road is horrendous but fun. I also saw some peacocks and an eagle. We climbs some big rocks where there were beautiful views.
title: Lots of elephants in Eco Park

body: Hurulu National Park boasts beautiful landscapes and wildlife, but my experience was significantly dampened by over-tourism. The excessive number of jeeps inside the park greatly detracted from the natural beauty and tranquility one would expect. The park management needs to limit the number of vehicles allowed at any given time and increase the presence of trained rangers to ensure a more sustainable and enjoyable experience for all visitors. While the park itself has the potential to offer a remarkable encounter with nature, the current situation with overcrowding needs urgent attention.
title: Overcrowded Experience at Hurulu National Park

body: We were surprised by the number of elephants that we saw here. The park is one of the smaller ones but the elephants roam free. We saw some on their own a family with a new born - about 3 weeks old and two smaller herds.The second one of around 11 elephants were almost in touching distance and carried on regardless of our proximity.A great trip out.
title: Elephant trip

body: This time we went on a safari here in the Eco Park. We hadn't known this one before. There weren't many tourists because it had rained heavily the day before. We really enjoyed the tour, also because of the many elephants ;))
title: Beautiful safari!

body: Our tour had a fascinating start, as we were able to watch two elephants drinking and eating with just one other jeep. The next elephant sightings were also a lot of fun, you really see a lot of these impressive, beautiful animals. However, after only about 40 minutes it became an increasingly unpleasant experience for me. The more jeeps came into the park, the more the elephants were harassed. As soon as elephants were seen, dozens of jeeps drove towards them. The jeep drivers reported the elephant sightings to each other via walkie-talkie and then it seemed as though all the jeeps within a 5-minute radius were racing towards them. Much too close, much too many and much too loud. When we harassed a mother elephant and her two young ones with 7 more roaring jeeps - I can't call it anything else, as the jeeps kept reversing to approach them again from a "better angle" when they had gone away - we asked our jeep driver to drive back. Instead of the planned 3 hours, we were in the park for about 1 hour. I regret not having read other people's experiences on Tripadvisor beforehand. Hopefully the way the elephants are treated at this park will change.
title: Something has to change here

body: we got to the top of a big rock to see the scenery and elephants, great views. there were not many elephants. tourists are overpriced
title: overpriced

body: You could see some isolated elephant herds. Something different experience than Minneriya National park and Kaudulla national park. In this herds are more or less 10 to 15. Another specialty is the Entrance fee is much cheaper than other two parks.
title: Elephant safari with a low cost.

body: We started the safari in the afternoon, the weather was rainy, but it was not a problem for us. We saw Sigiriya in the morning and went on the safari in the afternoon. I think our guide was able to give us a good experience. We saw elephants. Our diver took us very close. Yes. It is indeed a good experience.
title: Hurulu Eco Safari

body: What a remarkable safari!! We saw so many wild elephants, mums and calves, we even saw a bull elephant walking down the main road back. Such magical creatures, our driver was brilliant he got brilliant spots and if we spotted anything he stopped instantly, 100% recommend visiting here
title: Magical experience

body: Went in three jeeps. Thankfully the rain stopped. The tops were opened and we had a whale of a time. Saw a few elephants, peacocks, a variety of eagles and a few other birds. Sitting down in the jeep driven along the uneven roads gave the body a nice massage! Standing was a tad more comfortable one would say! Overall a lovely and very memorable experience.
title: Splendid!

body: A small national park located in Habarana. We saw many elephants. The stone hills are very beautiful and the surroundings can be seen very beautiful from the top of them. There is also a beautiful lake in this park. In addition to elephants, peacocks, eagles, monkeys and several other types of birds, we also saw the number of elephants and peacocks compared to The rest was more. This park has a very beautiful nature. It was very heartwarming to see baby elephants with their mothers.
title: Eco

body: This is well worth the visit, nothing more amazing than seeing the elephants in their natural habitat, the safari was a really memorable experience.. And we had the BEST driver !!
title: Well worth a visit !

body: A very interesting place to visit. We were lucky in that we saw approx 10 Elephants in total, plus Mongoose, Chameleon, Peacocks and some other beautiful birds. Scenery is quite spectacular. The drive in the back of a jeep is quite bumpy and could be hot; dont forget a hat and sunscreen..
title: A lovely Eco park

body: The elephant herds do move between three parks and at the time we visited they were in this park. We had a great view of the herd, along with the dozens of other vehicles as well.
title: Excellent for elephants

body: This park was proposed to us by Bangalawa resort owner where we were staying. We were not sure about this park. Our guide in the park was Asanka . His knowledge of the park and animals is amazing and he knew exactly where to take us. We saw approx. 40 elephants with some being max. 5 meters from out truck. Asanka really made our day and he is the person to ask for, if you want to have wonderful trip to the park.
title: Great park to see, with wild Elephants almost touching your. Just ask for guide Asanka and you will have great day.

body: We really enjoyed seeing groups of elephants in the park. We also saw a few birds. I believe there are other wild animals but we didn't see them. We had plenty of room (6 adults) to stand up and look out of the roof.
title: Great Eco park experience

body: I happened to visit the park by the recommendation of our wildlife guide Asanka, whom I sourced through TripAdvisor it self. The visit was purely to see the gentle giants (elephants), and it was interesting to see many in one go. Had an awesome time, and did take many photographs to. Wish I spent the whole day inside the park, I would have had the chance of seeing more than the gentle giants.
title: Amazing place to visit to see the gentle giant

body: We didn't expect much but boy were we mistaken. We spent there time from 2pm to 5pm after our trip to Polonaruwa. Guys at our hotel reccomend the place as there are three parks in proximity and the herds of elephants are migrating between them according to water availability. Obviously February was ideal time for this park. We saw around 50 elephants, lots of them basically almost touching our truck. Never seen something like this and strongly recommend to go there if you have a chance.
title: Hidden gem

body: We spent around three hours in Eco Park on an afternoon tour and met our first family group of six elephants after just 30 mins drive. The driver quietly manoeuvred our jeep into the scrub and the elephants just slowly wandered by only a few metres away. Through the whole experience we encountered numerous other groups of upto 15 elephants in the largest group, just wandering through small clearings in the dense woods. Our visit was late January so maybe we were fortunate as I understand they move between three different Parks throughout the year.
title: Wow great experience

body: We went on an afternoon safari from 3 to 6pm. We got very lucky and saw some single male elephants and a large herd of 18 elephants mostly female. We followed the large herd as they eat their way through the park. One elephant got within 5 feet of our jeep and was not bothered by us being there. It was a wonderful afternoon.
title: Elephant Park

body: Today we visited Hurulu Eco Park. unequivocally great experience! More than 15 wild elephants, water buffaloes, peacocks, monkeys and many birds. Only 3 jeeps set out on the morning route. My dream came true. Thanks a lot
title: My dream came true

body: Positive:- The park is very beautiful. Mostly jungle and bush. - The whole staff was very friendly. - The jeeps are in pretty good shape and a good way to ride around the park and take pictures.- Very fair price in my opinion.- After booking the Safari, i was contacted via WhatsApp. I could normally talk to this person and clarify any details regarding pick up, start-time etc.Negative: - Guide was completely unable to speak english, would have been nice to have someone tell just a couple facts or something about the park and the animals.- Have to buy ticket AND pay for the safari. None is included in the other.- Time promised was 3h, in reality it was more like 2 hours.
title: Very nice way to spend an afternoon in Sigiriya

body: We had a wonderful sunset safari tour. We saw elephants, horn bills, eagles and so much more. The guide stopped often to show us something he had spotted. We spent hours driving around, it was really special!
title: Sunset safari

body: This is good place to spot wild elephants very closely. However most people visit either Minneriya or Kaudulla national parks. But in some seasons elephants migrate to this eco park. So best to discuss with your guide or hotel personnel to check which park to visit . This is located very close to habarana junction and you can get a safari jeep from habarana itself. Jeep costs 3500. Entrance ticket prices vary depending on the people count. For 10 of us it cost 1456. We could see plenty of wild elephants during our safari. And one elephants tried to attack our Jeep. It was a thrilling experience. However you will only see elephants here. It’s very hard to see any other animal here.
title: Close encounters with wild elephants

body: We were really surprised by the number of elephants that roam around there.There were many sizes of elephants from small to big.There were small ones with their protective moms.I didn’t see any males ones but there were many females divided into groups.
title: Adequate amount of elephants

body: Originally we were going to Minneriya National Park,but was told it was closed? When we first got in the jeep and started off it felt like everyone was in a race, jostling for a spot to see the elephants. At our first sighting of elephants there ended up being sooo many jeeps it was just ridiculous and really spoiled the whole experience. However after this first sighting the jeeps seemed to spread out and our next few sightings were much more enjoyable with only a couple of other jeeps or no one else.We ended up seeing lots of elephants and it was very enjoyable watching them in their natural environment.
title: Lots of Elephants

body: This is a great national park with lots of wildlife. You'll tour the park in traditional open sided safari vehicles on dirt tracks, through scrub, open plains and water holes (watch out for spiky branches on the narrow tracks).There are a lot of elephants here so you're guaranteed to see them, and quite up close at times. There are a lot a lot of exotic birds too, which your guide will almost certainly spot and point out for you. You may also see other creature, such as land monitors, water buffalo and wild boar. It feels a lot like an African game drive without the predators. Near the end of the drive, there's a lookout platform at the top of a small hill that you can walk up to if you wish. Altogether absolutely great fun. When we visited at the start of March, it was relatively quiet in the park, but this may have been due to the impending pandemic.
title: Elephants...!!

body: What at first resembled an LA freeway at knock off time and after hanging on for grim life & being bounced from pillar to post , it became worth while ! You need to remember to duck as the open topped & sided Jeeps go thru the scrub & under trees & low branches ad nauseam !!! After what seemed forever on dusty & hot tracks we sighted our first pachyderm and the flood gates opened. We watched single males & mothers & calves & family groups wander & feed in the wild. Very exciting and in some cases came nearly nose to trunk with each other ! I actually felt sorry for the Elephants at some stages as a sighting ended with up to 10 jeeps surrounding the prey ! Got to see many birds, peacocks & water buffaloes and thoroughly enjoyed the experience. The bruises on my backside proof of a rough ride but worth it !!
title: Bumpy Start

body: Took a Jeep safari here and was not disappointed, came in the afternoon and saw lots of wildlife. Really recommend this park
title: Amazing

body: We wanted to visit Minneriya National Park to watch the wild elephant. Our guide/ driver told us that Minneriya National Park was flooded due to heavy rain. We then followed his recommendation to have our safari trip at Eco Park. Actually, we had a wonderful time at this park and managed to see quite a number of wild elephants in small herd including the elephant calves. There is a huge rock in the park where we climbed up (and can be done easily) to enjoy the greenery in the park where we could see some elephants from far too. We also saw a peacock and water buffaloes. Be prepared to get dusty due to the driving on the dirt road. There was a jeep which encroached to the young elephants that aggravated the mother elephant which turned aggressive as protective instinct for her loved ones. The respective jeep driver and guide were screaming and shouting trying to chase the mother elephant away which worsen the situation. Eventually, the particular jeep and tourist managed to escape from the mother elephant’s aggression, but the jeep was damaged by the elephant trunk and luckily there was no casualties in this incident. This gave a discounted experience as the elephants were kind of intruded which caused the ruckus. Additionally, there were conflicting information shared in TripAdvisor in term of the pricing for the entrance fee and jeep service. Hence, we are now confused if we had overpaid the service with LKR12,000 for 2 of us including jeep and entrance fee. Secondly, there was one sharing that the flood at the Minneriya National Park was a scam to bring tourists here instead. But there is no way to verify these information in the website and whatsoever. Our conclusion is that since we indeed had a good time, the rating should be 4-star minus the 1-star due to the confusing/ unclear pricing and information about the scam to detour the tourist from Minneriya National Park. Hopefully, the management should step in to clarify the confusion for all.
title: Great experience for the first time!!!

body: We were a little disappointed as we’d geared up for a visit to Minneriya park; this was ok and we did see several elephants very close up.
title: Interesting

body: We took a local tour guide & driver to see the elephants & other wildlife at Eco Park. I'd say the park itself may not be the best because of very long grass, lots of vegetation & not too many open spaces. Due to this it's hard to get a proper sighting & see elephants meandering along. We did still see a few small herds with babies which the adults would crowd around to protect when they obviously felt under threat from many jeeps descending to gawp at them.We also saw Eagles, many birds, water buffalo & a chameleon. The viewpoint your driver will take you to has a lovely panoramic view too.All in all it was good but not spectacular.
reviewer_location: Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park, United Kingdom
title: Enjoyable to spend a couple of hours.

body: Initially I was advised that I could engage a jeep at Hurulu Eco Park by paying the jeep charges at the ticket counter. However upon reaching there I was told by the staff at the ticket office that they dont provide the jeep and that I should hire one, have the jeep driver to stamp on a form , and only then I could enter the park after paying the entrance fee at the counter (a few thousand LKR). I went back to Habarana town, luckily Rana's Tours at Habarana quickly helped me with a 4WD drive car for LKR 5K or thereabout. The reason I chose Hurulu Eco Park was that the elephants were supposed to have moved from Kaudula / Minneriya to Hurulu owing to heavy rains in the first two. I went in at about 1.30 pm and for the first hour or so until , there were hardly any elephants, but later we saw dozens and dozens of elephants. the young ones were so so cute, and etched in my mind's eye. It was so lovely to see how their mothers are protective about their young. The tour last about 2 hours totally. They dont allow cars in the park, you must have or engage a jeep, the park authorities say 4WDrive is preferred but not a must. The park roads are quite bumpy even with the 4W Drive jeep it was rather bumpyThere were no other animals there and overall it was a very pleasant and enjoyable experience. It would be seriously good if the park authorities allowed for jeeps to be pooled to reduce disturbance caused by huge numbers to the elephants. Apart from this everything else was good.
title: Dozens of elephants with young ones

body: We saw dozens of wild elephants up close in the lush countryside with a knowledgeable and caring guide. The only off-putting thing is the dozens of jeeps like us all doing the same thing... we felt sorry for some of the elephants having so much attention from the humans. Nevertheless the scenery is stunning... exceptionally beautiful and the elephants are majestic.
title: Up close with wild elephants

body: We had originally planned to visit Kaudulla but following much rain in the area, it seems the elephants had moved to Hurulu. Whilst we did see a large number of elephants, many of these sightings were negatively impacted by the sheer number of jeeps quickly arriving and surrounding the animals. Action needs to be taken to restrict the number of jeeps entering the park and ensuring jeeps are carrying more than 2 passengers.I guess the issue is very much financially driven with more jeeps resulting in more money for both the park and drivers. However, this does need to be balanced with caring for the animals and environment rather than such large numbers of jeeps emitting significant noise and pollution.
title: Enjoyed seeing the elephants but far too many jeeps detracted from the experience.

body: We enjoyed our second visit to this park having been last year. We had a fantastic afternoon watching the elephants and enjoying the scenery. It is well worth the time but be prepared for very bumpy tracks that shake the bones of you.
title: Lovely Afternoon

body: Taking local advice on where the elephants were, we spent a beautiful afternoon in the Eco Park. Here the grass is tall and so the elephants are harder to see, and pop out of the high grass unexpectedly, which they did. Always take local advice and a fantastic experience is to be had, in a lovely landscape.
title: A wonderful safari experience

body: Had a great morning out, couldn't believe how close we got to the elephants! Definitely worth the 6am start!
title: Elephants in the wild'

body: We had a great driver who managed to find a family of about 5 elephants with a baby and we had them to ourselves for 5 mins before any other jeeps arrived. We also saw more elephants and birds on the safari. There is a viewpoint too which has great views of the park. I would definitely recommend this park. We were told that roads at Mineriya were impassable due to water so we went here instead.
title: Brilliant

body: Animals in the wild are an amazing site and none more so than elephants, so Hurulu is an absolute treat. To start with, there is a little bit of gridlock as lots of jeeps go off into the park in search of elephants. However, the park is so big, you are quickly out on your own or with, at most, two or three other vehicles. Then, if you are lucky enough to see elephants, your driver will get you close enough to see them eat and interact but far enough away to give them their space. Having said that, the animals are so chilled that they come pretty close and I defy anyone not to feel humbled and awestruck by these amazing creatures.Despite being in a four wheel drive jeep, it does get a bit bumpy so be prepared to hold on tight on occasion. You will need to set aside around three hours for your visit but it will be worth every single minute.Highly recommended.
title: Magical experience

body: Not the largest park you’ll ever visit, but if you want to see elephants in the wild, you’ll see lots. It’s difficult to drive 100 meters without seeing a herd. The largest we saw had 12, including two babies. You can get very close to the animals. In addition, you’ll see birds, the odd mongoose, and a snake to two. Two hours will more than suffice for a tour.
title: Easy Way to See Lots of Wild Elephants

body: We had a great jeep safari in the Eco Park. We drove for quite a while in our jeep before finding the elephants but, when we did, they were very close and lots of them. Our driver worked tirelessly to find them and did his very best to get us close for photographic opportunities. And then, when we thought our trip was over, he came across some more! So the 3 hours or so we spent bumping around in the safari was well worth it! Apparently they have moved the elephants from the Minneriya National Park to this area because of the lack of water in the latter. There is a viewing platform on a rocky outcrop and this is good to climb to see an overview of the whole area. A very successful trip!
title: Plethora of Elephants!

body: We were lucky in having a great driver but also the recommendation to get there before 3 when it gets crowded. We were one of the only jeeps out there. We were lucky enough to see probably 30-40 elephants and many babies too. You get incredibly close and with the engines off the silence apart from this magnificent creatures eating is humbling.
title: Brilliant, we were lucky and also go before 3

body: It’s not an Kenyan safari. It’s a drive with dozens of other vehicles fighting to surround a few elephants who are hard to see in the high grass. It’s elephants only and we got up close to them. It was sad as this was not nature in action but more of a drive around zoo. But, if you can’t go to Africa, then take the drive. $60 via hotel or $35 a person if you find one of many drivers around time.
title: Amusement Park Safari

body: We only saw a few elephants, and they were far away. The ride is rough and long but driving through the jungles is wonderful.
title: Very spread out but lovely

body: It was a sunny day we visited Hurulu Echo Park with friends. It’s much greener park these days with herds of elephants gathered feeding on grass and trees. Safari Jeep cruised along muddy off roads arching elephants and birds. It was such amazing tour with elephants standing close to vehicles. Two of the watching points o two large rocks provides a 360 degree view which is pleasing at the sunset. Although the tall bushes obstructs the full view of larger bulls , the sceneries are beautiful.Can recommend this lark for a half day visit......
title: Visit to Hurulu Eco Park

body: We had planned to do a safari at one of the two nearby national parks (Minneriya and Kaudulla), but there has been a lot of rain and flooding recently, so they were both not possible.This was an enjoyable option. We had a great driver and guide, recommended by our driver. It was fun, and entertaining, drive through the picturesque forest. We saw a handful of elephants almost immediately, but then it was a bit of a struggle to spot more. Through exchanges between the various drivers you could tell it was a bit of a frustrating day... But then we were treated to a few encounters with larger groups, including several adorable babies and juveniles. Because viewing was difficult the day we were there, when these herds were spited they were swarmed with jeeps. Still, the animals were mostly given amble room. Having only ever seen elephants in less than ideal circumstances - zoos, long ago circuses and the like, it was exciting to see the up close and in their natural environment. Entrance fees and payment to our guide were still quite affordable (roughly $60 US). Be aware that tickets can only be purchased with Sri Lankan rupees (no credit cards or USD accepted).The national parks promise the opportunity to see more animals, but under the circumstances this was very good.
title: Enjoyable option

body: This is a park you can definitely see wild elephants in the jungle. You can hire a safari jeep at the entrance where you buy the ticket. A must do for tourists to see wild Elephants
title: Elephants

body: Today I visited this park dated 29 Dec, 2019.too much people so many Jeep's, it's an average park inside only buffaloes and elephants.The entrance tickets for one person around 2400 and Jeep charges around 3000 to 3500.in this amount too much expansive.
title: Hurulu eco park

body: If you ve been for a safari in South Africa or Botswana you realise straight away that this is not gonna be what you signed up for.There is TONS of people crammed in a small park. When someone finds an elephant they signal the others who storm to the same place which quickly becomes more crowded than NY Times Square. At some point my wife and I joked that there are probably no elephants in the park and near the end they get one of them to parade in front of the keepse so tourists like us can take pictures.Having said that it's a real fun experience. You roam around a jungle (not dry dessert-like land like in South Africa). I would definitely do it again but make sure you understand it's more of an amusement park than an actual safari.
title: Not a safari but still worth it

body: We were quite unlucky with our trip. There was at least a 40 minute wait to get tickets organized at the entrance with what felt like 100s of other safari cars parked in a chaotic way trying to bottle neck through a tiny entrance. The roads were very muddy due to the amount of rain that had fallen and some cars got stuck which affected all the other cars who lined up one behind the other for at least 30 min. A huge traffic jam in nature! We asked our driver to bring us back to the hotel and only on the way back on the main road, with saw a small herd. The nature was beautiful. If you have done a safari in Africa, be ready for other expectations. The hotel explained only after that 2 other parks were closed due to the heavy rain so everyone comes to this one. There is only 1 entrance time available and that is at 13.30.
title: Totally overcrowded. Saw baby elephant with about 15 cars surrounding it

body: We found this trip very interesting for travellers with limited time available. Saw three herds of wild elephants and few species of birds. Ideal way to experience a mini safari.
title: Safari trip for two hours in Habarana

body: Very beautiful park. We saw a lot of elephants, birds and reptiles. The driver was very good and carefoul. We`ve seen some elephants very close to the jeep.
title: A place worth seeing

body: Great safari organised through our driver Hari from Chamila Tours. They chose the Park depending on where most elephants are at the time. Great truck that you could stand up in. Took a while to get into the park but enjoyed the bumpy ride and breeze. Not so bumpy that son fell asleep in the heat until we spotted our first group of Elephants. Great to see Elephant family groups in their natural habitat. Saw 4 large different groups, some very close, a few elephants spotted in bush. Baby elephants in most groups were soooo cuuuuute. Driver let us stay to watch as long as we liked. Got to get out and walk up to a look out. They are building a lake in front of the look out. Great park, recommended.
title: Baby Elephants

body: We booked "Safari with Asanka" through our hotel. There were 4 of us and we saw lots of elephants. More than 60 today. Even lots of babies and some tuskers too. We were really close. Many times only a few meters away. The park is beautiful with lots of different trees and granite boulders and grasses the elephants eat. Prepare to get jostled around. The roads are rough and boggy and there are plenty of tree branches scraping the top and sides of the jeep. This just adds to the authentic experience that it is! But hold on tight and keep your eyes open for when you need to duck. Apart from the many elephants we also saw lots of peacocks and several eagles as well. Our driver who was also our guide has an eagle eye and he found the animals for us so up close and personal and his attitude and respect towards the animals is so apparent and he speaks good English. He is knowledgeable and a funny guy too. The price was also better than other places we read reviews for at 5500 per person based on a group of 4 (minus a tip.) We all had such a great time and we were the last ones to leave the park. Even though it was now getting dark he stopped by every herd continuing out to the highway. Just a magical experience, what more can I say? Anyway you can contact Asanka through his Whatsapp # 0094770673470 if you wish to choose him as your driver. Thank you so much Asanka from your friends Blake and Darlin from Philippines
title: Totally exceeded or expectations a very memorable experience

body: We visited the park at around 230pm on 27 April and was delighted to see lots of elephants. Saw the elephants crossing the road few times and once a herd of 5-6 of them were just beside our Jeep! End of the tour, we stopped at a lookout point and there were about 10 of them around the area with one of them coming up the rock for water. The elephant was too close for comfort and I quickly walked up to the lookout point :) On the way back, we saw easily 10 more at the side of the main road with two of them drinking water from the tap of a well.
title: Encountered lots of elephants

body: The morning we were waiting for our guide and his jeep we taught that we are very unlucky since it started to rain a bit. The truth is - that was the best thing that could happen! It was raining but not too much, so almost all the elephants were out wondering through the park since the temperature was ideal for them. Until end of our trip (from 8am to 2-3pm) we saw more than 60 elephants and some birds and water buffaloes. Special thanks goes to our guide Rohan who was very well informed about the park and has a lot of interesting facts about Elephants plus his English is more than good. This part of Safari is very important, a lot of my friends had a guide who barely talked to them or told them anything about Sri Lanka and elephants in it. His phone number is +94773872750. We were at the park in the beginning of the February 2019th.Last and very IMPORTANT thing... There are many ways to see elephants in Sri Lanka, but please choose those which are the most natural. The best way to meet and understand elephants is to go to Safari and see them in their natural habitat. Please DO NOT EVER ride the elephant and support that kind of business. A lot of people don't care about those lovely creature and will do anything for hundreds of likes on Instagram. You should be smarter and more human than them! Enjoy your staying in this beautiful park and this beautiful island. Love Sri Lanka! P.S. If you want to see my pictures from this trip, you can find it on my instagram profile (@milesiztaleta)
title: One of the best experience in my life

body: We came to the park early morning on March and saw a lot of small groups of elephants eating grass a walking through park. Beautiful experience.
title: Private elephant watching

body: It cost 17,500 for 2 adults (£75 or so). The jeep was private, comfortable and clean. We had the driver and tour guide at the front, and me and wife at the back. It took about a 90-minute drive into the jungle until we saw any elephants, but then we saw maybe a couple of hundred scattered in different parts. Nothing to fault here really, the only problem was there were quite a few tourist jeeps wherever there were elephants, but it was still nice and everyone quietly enjoyed the nature.From start to finish all in all it took about 3 hours, you do get a break half way where you can climb up a small hill.
title: It's ok, not as good as I expected

body: Yes, you have a very good chance of seeing elephants here, but the way the safaris are run is awful.There were dozens of jeeps at every sighting, The poor elephants didn't know which way to turn. Some looked confused and had to make several attempts to find a way across the road.Not good for visitors either. With queues of jeeps those at the back could not see the animals.Not much other visible wildlife here either, except a few birds.There are plenty of other wildlife parks in this area and it's difficult to see how they could be worse.
title: Please go somewhere else. It's disgusting.

body: Yes, we saw only 5 elephants from a far and counted 52 safari jeeps. Honestly not worth the long hours and money. Maybe we should have started early in the morning to avoid the traffic jam within the park itself.
title: 5 Elephants and 52 Safari Jeeps

body: We took an afternoon safari here on February 26, 2019. The elephants had moved here due to rain in other areas had flooded their food. It was my first ever safari so not sure what to expect, but it was enjoyable. It seems like a balance, here but I think the jeeps pushed a little too close to one group of elephants by going off of the established roads. In several other locations we were able to stay on the roads and still see elephants close up. Tough balance.
title: Nice Park for an Afternoon Safari

body: After reading the reviews I was a bit worried about visiting the park. However, there weren’t too many jeeps when we were there and there were lots of elephants. The jeeps were respecting the elephants by turning their engines off and moving out their way. We had a lovely time and really enjoyed it! We all done safaris in Africa too so we’re pleased the experience was positive.
title: Saw lots of elephants

body: It was an excellent experience, although there was quite a lot of jeeps, like we were. But our guide was trying to pass them, so that we didn't ride like in a convoy. But were elephants were, there was always some jeep. Expect a lot of holes in the road, so the ride is not so smooth. We had a great sunny weather, with a nice sunset, so overall it was a great experience. But don't expect so much other animals, besides elephants. We saw some owls, parrots, peacocks, ets.
title: Elephant safari

body: We felt terrible but asked our driver to take us back to the car park, we couldn’t take the Kandy style traffic ram of jeeps all attempting to see the scant wild life in this park. Yes we saw a lovely family group of elephants but that was it, no birds, no monkeys just jeeps. The fumes alone were enough to make us want to finish this horrible experience, in fact the highlight was seeing a lead elephant get fed up and made a momentary gesture of annoyance to a jeep coming in the opposite direction (almost as if she was saying you are going the wrong way down a one way street). We felt ashamed to be a part of this, it is not the way to operate a business where wild animals are at stake. I have only given the mark of 2 blobs because I felt sorry for our driver, it was not his fault and just his job. Also some of the landscape was lovely and we had to keep thinking we are being very spoilt to find fault but it really was awful. I would not recommend this to anyone, we saw two beautiful elephants along our route on the main highway, along with multiple monkeys and even dogs and puppies were free to roam without the horror of this crowded tourist trap.
title: Maybe we’re spoilt

body: Don't expect Kruger, but it is worth visiting in a jeep for a couple of hours to see some elephants close up and a lot of birds. Don't be put off by the number of vehicles, they seem to help each other and take turns to give everyone a good view and they spread out after a while. You can get out to climb a small hill to get a view. Our trip was $40 per head for everything, except the "official guide" who decided to come with us, but his spotting skills were phenomenal and worth his tip.
title: An interesting experience

body: Jeep Fees: LKR 6500 (No receipts so may find something cheaper as well)Entry Fees: LKR 5000 for two roughly (For this you are provided a receipt so these are fixed)The park is huge. There are lots of jeeps running around and they do coordinate with each other. But when it comes to "cornering" an elephant or a herd i have seen max 5 jeeps around. So its not as bad as other safaris in Sri Lanka. We saw quiet a few elephants of various sizes. None with tusks though.There is a huge rock where all jeeps meet for a get together and this is the only spot where you can get down. Climbing up the rock gives you good view of the vastness of the jungle. Once you are here, the safari is almost coming to an end. Also, the jeep drivers sometimes provoke the elephants to create thrilling experience for the travelers. (This is my interpretation of what i saw; i may be wrong).Tips: If going in the afternoon, cover your head and arms properly. Its very hot and the heat bites. Carry sufficient water.If the jeep approaches a herd which has babies, be alert and take shelter in the jeep as the bigger elephant may run behind the speeding jeep to chase you away.
title: Good spotting of elephants

body: We saw 19 elephants in total and enjoyed the breeze in lovely viewpoint tower near the exit. If you’re ever feeling boxed in by the other jeeps just ask your guide to move on to a new area. This worked out well for us because it gave the elephants more space/less stress and we had our own intimate encounters with several other groups of elephants (with babies!) just down the side roads. Plenty of elephants for all to see... from a safe and peaceful distance!
title: Beautiful elephants abound!

body: We received a recommendation from our host at The Green Village Dambulla to visit the Hurulu Eco Park as it had the best chance of seeing Elephants. The other 2 National parks nearby had too much water levels and therefore not a good place to visit.Our host arranged a local independent jeep driver, Nadeesha from Lalith Jeep Safari.We quite simply had an amazing day out, just the two of us and a driver. When we arrived at the park, Nadeesha spoke with a park ranger and next minute the ranger jumped on our jeep and spent the next 3 hours with us. The ranger, Milton had great knowledge on the behaviour of the elephants and we never felt that we were in any danger, even when we had 6 elephants and 2 babies 6 foot from us. Milton knew all the good places and small tracks were and gave us a running commentary of all the wildlife. Nadeesha was a brilliant driver and never crowded the animals, always turned off his engine and allowed the elephants to approach the jeep, never chasing them. we were completely confident in his abilities as a driver and he clearly cared about the welfare of the animals. Milton, the ranger was one of 14 rangers in the park. Sometimes there are hundreds of jeeps in the park in the late afternoon, so we were lucky to spend some time with him. We arrived at the park at around 1pm and for the first hour we only saw another 10 jeeps, but later on the volume of jeeps increased. We had an unforgettable experience, we saw over 50 elephants, some as close as 6 foot away, we spotted a tusker, pregnant females and babies as young as 7 days old, all really close. The advantage of having a ranger with us was that if other jeeps got to noisy of frightened the elephants , Milton would tell them off and remind them to back off if they got too close and act responsibly. We liked the fact that the elephants were never really chased or surrounded too much, but you cannot get away from the fact that sometimes there are more jeeps than elephants.I would highly recommend Nadeesha (Email lalithsafaridambulla@gmail.com). We had an unforgettable day out.
title: Amazing day out with Lalith Jeep Safari

body: The large number of jeeps as the entrance fill you with dread about what is to come but the jeeps stay on the tracks and the elephants have plenty of places to go and don’t seem bothered by the swarms. Our driver avoided the temptation of sticking with the pack and managed to be the only jeep with a family of six elephants.
title: Don't be put off

body: I went in February. I think what I experienced there happens in most of the other parks close by like Minneriya or Kaudulla. Anyways he driver decided in which park the most elephants were expected. The few elephants there were surrounded by eight jeeps or more. The problem is that they don’t fill up the jeeps with people so there is mostly one Jeep per person or per couple. I understand that people need jobs here, but this is not a sustainable way and there are better systems in other National Parks. Jeeps crowd chaoticly around an elephant and sometimes the driver couldn’t get through or just drives by because there is no space to stop. Fumes and noise from the jeeps were constantly around me. I saw more animals outside in the country than in this NP. Not sustainable activity, no animals or nice nature observed, dusty, hot, polluted and crowded with people and Jeeps. Not recommended at all.
title: Bad!- More jeeps than animals

body: Our plan included jeep safari in Minnerwa national park, but due to migration of animal we were taken to Eco park. It was very busy with aith jeeps and if they had a good view would not move. I Can not animal were distressed. But it is impossible for wild life to have peace with that many tourists and jeeps. I felt sorry for animal and against my beliefs.we had to give a large tip to the driver and there was a ranger in our jeep we should have tipped him too for something which we did not enjoy
title: More a zoo than safari

body: We told our private driver to organize a safari tour for us. He organized a very nice jeep driver, i can't remember his name, but he always took his time so we could watch everything, there was no stress like in other jeeps. We started in the afternoon and it was very hot. But after an hour or so we saw our first elephants. Unfortunately there were many other jeeps with motors running, but our driver waited for them to leave and we had a lot of time to watch the elephants and take some pictures. It was a nice experience even though there were many many jeeps around.
title: You will see Elephants

body: There is no getting away from the fact that this can be a noisy and bumpy experience as a string of jeeps going off-road along rutted tracks heads off in search of elephants. But for us, seeing the elephants in their natural habitat, entirely unfussed by these curious tourists in the their noisy vehicles, was a highlight of our trip to Sri Lanka. Our driver Sameera (sourced by our wonderful guide Mr Daya: dayagunarathne@gmail.com who was provided by our equally wonderful travel agent demin@ceylanvacations.com) was excellent, seeming to have a 6th sense for where the elephants would be and where they might go next. We must have seen about 30 elephant in the park but the highlight was probably on the road driving home when we stopped to see a family of elephants browsing on trees at the roadside, coming within feet of our parked-up jeep.
title: Herds of elephants, and a herd of jeeps but very much worth it!

body: This visit was included in our trip by Kuoni, we had planned to visit Minneriya, but were switched to Hurjlu because of the elephants location. it was a total nightmare! I counted 45 jeeps all tying to get in front of each other along narrow tracks to drive up to the 10 or 12 elephants that were present in the bush with drivers completing with each other and blocking other jeeps. To see anything you need to stand up in the jeep while it was bouncing about on the dirt track. At one point a Jeep ahead of us reversed into our jeep resulting in a cut knee.Thankfully the elephants were the only unconcerned present and carried on eating the bush.This is tourism at its worst no control, planning or organisation and a misrepresentation of Eco principles.
title: A KEYSTONE COPS EXPERIENCE

body: We hired a jeep from mihin hotel for Rs 3500. We paid Rd 1500 as entrance fee. We were provided with 5 water bottles by mihin .We started our journey around 11 am. That time only 2 jeeps were with us. It was awesome . They take us near to elephants . I think elephants are Adjusted to this tourism. They don't care . It's only elephants' park. There are not any other animals. Few peacock live in the parkThere were many baby elephants and tuskers. We had lunch at mihin hotel. It was plain.quite ok. Not expensive.
title: Huge herd of elephants & tuskers

body: We realised this 'safari' might not be good as we waited in a queue of jeeps, similar to that of planes on the runway at Heathrow, to start the trip. Unfortunately our suspicions were confirmed. The first group of elephants we came across was surrounded by a circle of 20+ jeeps all jostling for position with their engines running. The elephants were clearly distressed by this. I found the whole situation upsetting and told the driver I did not want to continue the trip and asked that we return. This request was ignored and we continued racing through the park not sticking to the tracks but driving anywhere thus ruining the elephants habitat and that of any other fauna (not that we saw anything else). There is nothing remotely eco about this park and I would not recommend it to anyone.
title: Dreadful

body: Fantastic experience, sadly there are a lot of jeeps flying round searching for the same groups of elephants, but Rasika managed to avoid the crowds and we got incredibly close to several groups of elephants. Not only elephants, but he sought out different birds and other animals too! His English was ok, but more than good enough to poont out different animals and give us their names.We booked in advance from England on a website, but could have got it cheaper if we had booked it through our hotel.
title: Safari with Rasika

body: Our hotel arranged a driver and jeep for our trip in the park. It was certainly a budget ride, as it didn't last as long as those advertised. He drove around the park, found elephants and then brought us home again. This was fine with us. I had carted a heavy camera with a good zoom, so that I could spot the creatures. I needn't have bothered, as we were almost close enough to touch them!
title: Our first experience of seeing elephants in the wild.

body: Minneriya National Park was flooded so everyone seemed to be in Eco Park.Every elephant was surrounded by 20 to 30 jeeps in an unregulated,diesel fume scrum.Dont bother.
title: When they say jeep safari, they really are talking about the jeeps not the elephants

body: There was no question that the park had many elephants, but there were definitely more jeeps than elephants making it very unpleasant be part of. The whole area was covered in dust aroused by loud jeeps racing to get the best view for their clients. The drivers were shamelessly getting too close to the elephants making it feel like these animals were in a zoo.Not recommended for people who have been on a real safari in Africa.
title: More jeeps than elephants

body: Had some time to kill so our driver suggested a safari at Hurulu - a mate of his had a jeep so we reckoned it would be a good thing to do as a safari was 'on our 'list'. So many vehicles all following the same path without any regard for the elephants - really disappointing. It was unfortunate that the other local parks were closed due to flooding. We should have realised that on that basis everyone would be flocking to Hurulu. We did see elephants but we felt we did NOT need to be so close to them - far more exciting to see them from afar and in a more natural environment.
title: M25 at a standstill - springs to mind!

body: We almost didn't go to see the elephants as we had had several previous elephant experiences..... but then we thought we should. Compared to our previous experiences this was not so good. Our jeep driver took off at speed over very rough terrain. We were thrown about and had to hold on for dear life! When elephants were spotted there were at least 10 jeeps jostling to get far too near to the elephants. We did see about 30 elephants at different times but felt that given the number of jeeps packed around the elephants this was not the best experience we have had. We were ready to leave early having seen enough and absolutrly exhausted from having to hang on to the jeep to avoid injury!
title: Lots of jeeps to ambush elephants

body: after a dodgy start with 20 jeeps converging on 2 bull elephants and some unsavoury driving by some, it settled to be a sensible safari with plenty of elephants up close but not intruded upon. fabulous creatures, good size park and just awesome to watch. not hurried, good value. reccommended
title: Brilliant

body: We asked some drivers in which park the best wild spot opportunities were and this time it was in Hurulu. You pay for a 4WD and seperate tickets at the entrance. We had a very unexperienced driver and he was driving in the park like on the main road. Always want to be the first... damaging half the park with is f#*ked up driving style. It was much to busy and ECO was not one second an issue. On one moment tree or four elephants were grazing and 26!! 4WD surrounded them with a bunch of crazy people to fill their facebook and instagram accounts. At the end we went up a hill and when we came down a strange guy was standing at our car telling he was the owner and he needed more money. The driver acting as if he don’t know nothing about it. He try to force us by telling us to vissit us in our hotel to get his money. The driver act like he was his real bos. When we got angry they gone and we never heard about it. Never pay extra money and ask for a bill if you pay something. A 4 WD is about 4500-5000 rps for 3 hours.We were very disapointed about this park. Despite there was a lot of wildlife we feld like intruders and in for instance udawalawe we had a driver who feld responisible for the nature and most of the time we where alone.
title: OMG what is this

body: There are several elephant refuge parks in this area of Sri Lanka - you chose the one you go to by where the elephants are currently. Our driver asked around and, for us, it was Eco Park. The roads are seriously rough and you really do need the big 'jeeps' they use to go there. It's not dear to hire your own jeep and driver rather than be packed in with a group. Over the course of the afternoon we saw 39 elephants and also spent some pleasant time just sitting quietly up on a large rock outcrop and enjoying the scenery. (You'll probably see wild elephants crossing the roads in this area too). There were a lot of jeeps in the park (50+?), but they were generally pretty good in that they weren't pushing in too close to the elephants and were 'sharing' access when groups were found. It's not peaceful (except when there are elephants nearby when everyone goes quiet and the jeep engines are turned off), and there are plenty of people around, but it's a good enough way to see wild Asian elephants without annoying them too much.
title: Elephants in the wild

body: You should get to see elephants, although nothing like the numbers we have seen in Botswana. Nevertheless we saw several small groups of mothers with young and they are certainly always fascinating to watch. We went into the park about 1.30pm and it got progressively busy as the afternoon progressed. It did become a bit of a frenzy by the end with several jeep loads of tourists at a sighting, all trying to get the perfect shot!We also saw lots of varieties of bird including two species of eagle and lots of chameleons - three or four different types. That combined with the variety of trees and plants made it a great afternoon activity for us, but if you’re only interested in elephants you might not see large groups of them. The guides are knowledgeable about where they hide out and they share the information with each other so you should be in luck.
title: Elephants in the wild

body: I would not believe you could get so close to elephants in their natural habitat but you can at Eco Park. We had a wonderful driver who understood the etiquette of waiting your turn, not blocking other views and turning off your engine when static.For best results, try and stay as late as possible- we were rewarded with an encounter with a family of 8 elephants- shared w only one other jeep.Brilliant!
title: Fantastic

body: The park is ok and we did see close-up elephants. Unfotunately we went out of the jeep 10 minutes and the driver stoled some money out of our bags. Unfortunately we did notice only on our way back to kandy. You should avoid tours with Akila Village&Lake adventure - driver's name was Santa/Sampath or close to that)
title: Robbed by the driver - Akila Anuradha tour

body: There seems to be no limits with the amount of safari tours allowed to be happening at the same time. Our first contact with the elephants was with around 15 other jeeps. The drivers clamber around to try and get their customers the best view so go off the track - so much so two jeeps got stuck in the mud. Doesn’t feel respectful to the animals and we felt bad for being part of it. We also opted to have a guide with us - his English was poor so we couldn’t communicate much and learnt nothing from him.
title: Lots of elephants but too many jeeps

body: We were supposed to go to Minneriya Wildlife Park but our tour guide ripped us off by taking us to this park instead (we were not aware of this until we left the park). The park was so crowded with jeeps but they were hardly any elephants. We did not spot any other animals there.
title: Disappointing!

body: ...so I cannot compare but I believe African safari must be much richer in experience. We spotted only elephants here and it is also said that this park only "offers" elephants but there was no other choice in the area in this season as elephants already migrated from Minneriya here.First, I was terrified at seeing so many jeeps at the entrance to the park (at about 2 pm) but later in the park they all quite spread out and it doesn´t seem to be that crowded. We saw several groups of 5-6 elephants, always accompanied by some other jeeps. Finally, we managed to have also our "private" experience when we found 4 elephants and no other jeep around and that is what we enjoyed the most.The bathrooms are available at the entrance so make sure to use them as guides don´t want to let you out of the jeep - they´re afraid of being attacked by animals.
title: My first safari

body: This Safari was almost a complete disappointment. We had seen 5 peacocks, an eagle and a monkey an hour and 15 minutes into the safari. If your over 5 ft tall you cannot see our if the Jeep without standing up the whole way. Just about when I was ready to give up we saw roughly 50 elephants towards the end of the tour. If you like elephants. This is definitely for you. If you’re looking for diversity’s and a sitting Jeep...go to Yala.
title: Elephants and.....elephants

body: We started at 5:30 am from our hotel. Reached by 6am at the Eco Park. We were the first to enter. The mist of the dawn, the feel of the forest, and the anticipation to see the wild life peeping from an open four wheel drive awakened the curious child in all four of us - including me and my wife.When we saw the herd of elephants crossing a small pathway - it was a scene worth narrating. Those animals communicate and you can see it so clearly. This experience is worth the early morning prep for the wild.
title: Wake up with the wild

body: We were lucky enough to go to Africa on safari recently and so we're not sure if we would go on this as we were a bit safaried out, however glad we did as seeing elephants in the wild is always mesmerising! You will see elephants but not much else, as long as you are aware of this, you should enjoy it We decided to go at lunch time and were pleased we did as there were only a few jeep about... On our return ( just before 3.00) we went past the start point which was now packed with jeeps! I don't think we would have enjoyed it as much with all those jeeps as there must have been so much conjestion which would impact the experience and probably not great for the elephants either. Top tip... Go at lunch time!
title: Saw lots of elephants, make sure you avoid peak times

body: As with any safari its always a fantastic experience to see animals in their natural habitat, especially majestic creatures such as elephants, which we did see several. I personally found our driver quite respectful but we did see other jeeps getting far too close in my opinion and crowding the elephants in to get a closer look. Also saw some great birds and a wee chameleon too! We also got stuck in the mud at one point but thankfully our driver managed to get us out eventually, its would seem none of the jeeps are properly equipped to deal with such a scenario which is a concern (esp as all the other jeeps following us turned around and left us in the mud!)
title: Elephants!

body: Due to minneriya and kaluda parks being closed we visiting hurulu instead to see elephants. We did see lots of elephants, some very close to the vehicle. However, there were no rules to stop the Jeeps getting too close to the elephants - they were driving all over the place to get close to the herd. Felt a little like we harrassing the elephants due to the sheer number of vehicles. This park may well be quieter and nicer when minneriya and kaluda parks are open.
title: Lots of elephants but jeeps everywhere

body: If you are a fan of safari and you like adventure this is a good option. Very wide jungleJeep safariReal safari feelingOnly elephants and some birdsIt ll shake your brain But , should be done.
title: Hard and enjoy full

body: Went to this elephant Safari as others are not accessible due to heavy rains. Saw lot of elephants include small 3-4 month babies. Jeep ride is very bumpy, should avoid if you have back/neck problems.
title: Excellent elephant Safari!!

body: Quite bouncy in the jeep with our 18m old, though. We saw 40+ wild elephants. Highly recommended :-)
title: Great. Saw many elephants in the afternoon.

body: Although at first the trip was quite fun, we counted at least 40 jeeps bumper to bumper driving into the forest. When we saw an elephant, jeeps would crowd round as close as possible, often penning the animal in, just to get the best picture. The air quickly filled with the smell of exhaust fumes. Hardly an eco park. Some of the other tourists were shouting at the animals to get their attention, and at their driver to get closer. Little respect for the animals.
title: Not very animal friendly

body: We had a wonderful experience in the park once we got past the very long ticket line. So many elephants were there, including babies. It was magical! The only thing that was a slight bummer was seeing jeeps driving way to close to elephants to the point where it clearly bothered them.
title: Beauriful experience

body: We went on a jeep safari at 2 p.m. There were around 50 to 60 jeeps bumper to bumper in the muddy paths with some jeeps trying to overtake others. The forest smelt like diesel the whole 2.5 hours we were there. We saw may be 4 or 5 elephants but the traffic jam is what I will remember. I suspect early mornings would be a better time to go. I felt sorry for the elephants and for ourselves. Quite a ripoff at 5000 LKR per person.
title: Terrible for elephants and people

body: We did see elephants, we did enjoy the fresh air while driving thru the park in open safari vehicle. This, like ALL safari parks and experiences in Sri Lanka, are woefully overcrowded and suffer from overtourism #overtourism and bad overuse practices. The safari companies and hotels and guesthouses book only "private" safaris. So, even if you are a party of 1, you go by yourself in a large jeep that can easily fit 4. If you are a party of 2, you go just you two in a large jeep that can easily fit 4. Make friends at your guesthouse and book a safari for 4. Or, park should match up travelers upon arrival, and have each jeep go full with 4 persons. This would not only save travelers money, but most importantly, help curb overtourism and vehicle crowding in the park(s). Horribly bad as 15 vehicles would stop at the same elephant or animal, wait there for 10+ minutes, then all proceed together, and then all stop again together at the next sighting... awful. As tourism grows in Sri Lanka, it will absolutely destroy the environmental, visual, and aesthetic natural treasures and national parks it has... Hurulu eco Park, Minerya National Park, Yala National Park, Uda Walawe National Park. This could easily be solved by:(a) Combining 4 tourists per jeep. (b) have staggered entry times (c) have rule that no more than 5 jeeps at a time viewing/photographing animals. (d) have jeeps keep to a time limit of 5 minutes of viewing and photographing and then move on.
title: We Did See elephants. Only a Fair Safari Experience. Improvements Needed

body: Great experience to see these glorious animals up close and personal.Herds happily meandering through the bushland, young in tow.As has been noted, far too many vehicles jostling for position.In fairness to the drivers of the 4WD vehicles, they did their best to afford everyone an opportunity to see what they came for.If there is a quieter time to visit, ask your guide to recommend the best viewing times to avoid 'rush hour' and plan around this.I would love to give this place a score of 5/5 but it scores a 4/5 because of over exploitation
title: Up close and personal with elephants in their natural habitat

body: I think December is the best time to visit this park.Be at the park gate by 2.00 pm. You can see elephants at a very close range. They crossed the road just in front of our jeep a few feet away. The viewpoint on the small mountain provides a spectacular view of around.Guide Malan was good. Provided information on the park, animals and places within the park. Got to see about 40 elephants in small herds around 5-10 with small calves.Value for Money ....
title: Elephants !!!

body: We were lucky enough to see several groups of elephants .Lots and lots of babies .They crossed the road in front of us so there were several opportunities for pictures. What I did not enjoy is the number of jeeps inside the park at some point I felt that we were harassing the poor animals .In fact one of them got annoyed while protecting his baby abd tried to attack a jeep .
title: Elephants! Elephants!

body: Minneriya and Kaudulla were close because the lake water level was too high and jeeps couldn’t go inside. Hurulu eco park is still part of Minneriya. So I was imagining Hurulu had a vast open area with a lake similar to the other two. But it doesn’t have any water area where all animals come and drink (or at least, the route my jeep took didn’t have it). It’s just pretty much all bushy jungle. So when I saw elephants afar, all I could see was their grey backs moving (?) above bushes. The first of all, I went there at a wrong time 12pm lunch time. Apparently their lunch time is from late afternoon. A good thing was only 2 jeeps. Obviously, the downside was very few elephants. My Jeep encountered a small herd of elephants crossing a jeep path very closely. But I just felt the feel of enclosed environment rather than big safari. I was a solo traveler. I saw a jeep shop on a steet and arranged it by myself. The jeep itself costs 3000 rupees. I can’t remember the entrance fee but it’s stated on their website. Plus, some service fee on top of the entrance ticket to the park and jeep entrance fee. The accommodation everyone stays in this area can arrange those for you. Apparently you pay handling fee on top. It is up to the individual if you see this rip off or saving your effort to shop around by spending your time. When my jeep entered the park, one man wearing Hurulu eco park shirt getting on my jeep without telling me anything. He turned out to be a volunteer park guide. It’s a FREE service (you can give him tips if you are happy). His English was ok-ish even though most of the time, he replied to my questions by just saying ‘ok, ok’. It was nice to have him in the end as a company otherwise it would’ve been super boring jeep ride by myself. The only thing put me off was when the jeep bumped, he tried to hold my waste to support many times even though I told him I didn’t need this. One point, he was rubbing my elbows for nothing. That was quite disgusting.
title: If you can go to Minneriya or Kaudulla park, you should go there instead.

body: We were booked to go to Minneriya national park, but our driver advised we come here as more elephants on this park, and he was right, we got so close you could almost touch, it was fantastic to sit and watch the mums and dads with their young, how they protect them when the jeeps come along the track, dad dusting baby down with the soil , to keep them cool. It is an unforgettable experience, a good few hours spent.
title: Elephant haven

body: We were there during off season so did not get to see many elephants. The jeep ride was a good experience. Driver tried to push us off as Sri Lanka citizens to evade the tourist ticket charges but didnt work. We waited almost an hour for matters to be sorted out before out journey into the forest actually started.

body: Forest looked very beautiful as it was soon after some rainy season. Lot of green around. We could see a large number of Elephants including very small babies. Jeep ride was good and we could enjoy the full off road expereince as it was muddy and we got stuck half a way.
title: Hundreds of Elephants

body: Safari to see wild elephants - the best place to see them at this time of year. Great tour excellent driver plenty of opportunities to see wild elephants and good value for money compared to others around the area!
title: Great visit !

body: The best thing is to see the generations ie lots of elephant calves of different ages. It was low season so only about 6 jeeps josling to get close (our driver was awesome).Other birdlife etc there as well - but I was only focussed on the elephants. It is on dirt roads ie not really off track.
title: Heap of elephants

body: We skipped Minneriya Safari Park to choose this one instead - on the recommendation of our Driver. Great choice. The Park is large , dry for the most part and with a lot of scope for Off Roading !! The Rules state that Jeeps must be open roofed...which is great but the sun can be really sharp. Best time to enter is around 2-3 pm or so, considering that Elephant sightings are best around 4-5 pm. We saw more than 20 of them in groups at different places. No other wildlife as such.Lots of Bird species. Jeep drivers are good at Off Roading and go really close to the Elephants--Which is not necessarily a great thing ..but whatever. Overall an Afternoon well spent.
title: So Many Elephants !!

body: In habarana area there are 3 main parks for elephant watching. Minneriya, kaudulla and hurulu park are those. Time to time elephants migrate from one park to another. During our visit it was hurulu park. Park is not that huge but we could see about 30 40 wild elephants. The safari took about 3 hours. Evening time is more preffered to see elephants.
title: Great place to see wild elephants

body: It was a novel and unique experience for us, going on safari. Great feeling to feel the wind through our hair (and to be in the 4x4), as we drove to the park, and we were fortunate to see several groups of elephants.
title: Great fun

body: best place to do safari good . service good and luxury jeep .. nice nathure jeepes price better than other agient
title: safari

body: Great place to view elephants in their natural habitat. We hate reading reviews on the elephant rescues that don't take care of the animals. This is how it is supposed to be for the elephants.
title: Amazing elephants

body: We were told this was where 'the gathering' of elephants was. Our guide wanted us there early and we could see why as there was chaos at the gate with dozens of jeeps clamouring to get in. It was our first Sri Lankan safari and we had Bird watchers with us but if we stopped another jeep would go past scaring whatever wildlife we were looking at. Watching another jeep getting stuck in the mud and the antics to get it out was amusing but we all finally got to the elephants. There were around 40 - 50 elephants feeding at the lakeside with around 70 jeeps surrounding them - not quite the wildlife experience we'd hoped for. We were there over the christmas holidays so probably much busier than usual.
title: Elephants

body: Huluru is just a temporary solution for the rainy season (Autumn months), when the elephants have left Minneriya. Do not go there during any other time, Minneriya is the best place to see animals and enjoy year round, as every jeep driver with testify. Do not trust local companies that tells you otherwise.
title: Worst park in the area

body: Was expecting to see a village of elephants together, as mentioned in other reviews and the tour agent. But they were just 3-4 at a time. However we enjoyed it. Especially my daughter
title: Expected more of it, still enjoyable

body: The eleohants were certainly here! Saw an amazing group if 50 together towards the end if our afternoon safari. Not to mention many birds including a hawk eagle.
title: Great safari

body: It's a elephant heaven, it's used as a temporary stay while moving from Kaudulla National Park to Minneriya,
title: Hurulu Park

body: This is a mad made park but can see elephants most of the time of year. We went there 2-3 times & every time we visited able to see them. Not a quite adventure safari when you compare with other parks in Sri Lanka
title: Not quite natural but can see elephants

body: Excellent Safari with local guy. Tour lasted about 3.5 hours. Hundreds of Elephants came out of jungle heading for grass and water,
title: Excellent

body: I visited this park in april. its on of the few national parks in srilanka where you get to see elephants in a close distance. However except the elephants it's incredibly difficult to see other animals such as leopards and jackails since its a dense forest. At times it gets very interesting. Once one huge bull elephant got annoyed by our presence and started chasing all the jeeps when everyone got close to him. Its better if all the drivers could act responsible.
title: Elephants galore !!

body: Difficult seeing the indian elephants at first, but ended up seeing a whole family plus a leopard in a tree! Bumpy ride, but worth to see the beautiful nature of Sri Lanka.
title: Elephants and a leopard!

body: What a great experience. Managed to get up close to several of these majestic beasts in their natural environment. Beautiful to see.
title: Amazing drive to get close to these beautiful creatures.

body: Best place to sight elephants during monsoon and can do some bird watching..I recommend to do a safari early in the morning or late in the evening.
title: Elephant Paradise !!!

body: This is the place Elephants gather during the monsoon period and after that till the conditions are right so they can move to Minneriya and Kawdulla national park. Always advise your safari drivers not to go too close, you are seeing the largest land mammal in asia, so no need to go under their trunk and face the repercussion.
title: To see the Elephants during wet seeson

body: If its wild elephants you want to see you will see plenty here & at very close range. We were lucky & had a very good driver & guide. Well wprth the effort.
title: Elephants galore

body: It was our first safari on Sri Lanka and I was very excited to see elephants but... I felt very guilty after all as jeep drivers seem to not have any respect to animals and nature. One of them got too close to group of elephants with baby. Elephant's mother got really upset and started chasing all cars in the area including ours. The situation seemed to be pretty dangerous and luckily no human or animal got hurt but it made me think that people shouldn't go there if they cannot respect wildness of nature...
title: Safari

body: Had a great time. Saw loads of elephant's and even a tortoise. This park is well placed for Habarana accomodation, only 15 minutes away and reasonable entrance fee.
title: Safari

body: We were recommended to go to this park on our safari as the elephants had been seen there recently however I believe this can change regularly so ask your tour guide. After a 4 hour jeep drive we must have seen at least 35 elephants and a whole range of birds. Well worth paying for a jeep safari in these national parks.
title: Elephant safari

body: Went on a prearranged jeep safari with family at Horulu Eco Park which is supposed to be part of the larger Mineriya National Park. We went on a 2 hr safari in the morning between 7 am and 9 am. Was totally disappointed as we could not sight a single animal except a bird or two. Not even the elephants which are the most commonly seen animal by tourists. It was a sheer waste of time and money.
title: Not much to see

body: We wanted to visit other park nearby but we were recommended to go here because elephants shoud be there. It was true, there were plenty of them in small group also eith young ones. We saw like 6different group and stopped and I had the feeling we didnt bother them. Totally recommended if you have info from locals that elephants are over there.
title: Many elephants

body: The Eco park is a lovely all natural place to see elephants. Unfortunately you can see little else. I went on a tour with a popular local tour operator and although I had no warden I was with a group of jeeps that had a couple with them. body: We organised a jeep and driver through our homestay and we had the most magnificent time.At first I thought we were not going to see any elephants, but finally we came across some, and from then on there were so many, it was amazing.The jeeps turned their engines off whilst we stopped to watch the elephants graze, and what a beautiful sight it was to see.The baby elephants were a highlight, they are so cute!It was quite hot getting around in the open top jeep, so make sure you have a hat and sunscreen.Whilst I recognise people feel that this safari ruins the natural habitat, our driver stuck to the roads and paths, I felt he was very respectful to the elephants.An amazing experience!

body: We visited Hurulu Eco Park in April during the local New Year week and the timing was superb in terms of number of elephants visible. However as others have mentioned previously, as soon as a herd is spotted a convoy of jeeps descend on the area and everybody gets boxed in and the elephants tend to pass through quickly strtled by the nosie. That said, our driver was pretty good after a while at escaping the crowd and finding elephants away from the rest of the jeeps including a memorable moment when we parked near a waterhole as two elephants passed by very close to the jeep. All in all a great experience although extremely hot at this time of year.
title: Great time of year to see the elephants

body: Planned to go to Mineria but our driver said the elephants wll have wandered over to Eco park this late in the season. Was a bit sceptical but he hadn't let us down so far. On the times other drivers caught up with us, they always left our path clear and the elephants didnt pay any attention to us. All in all a good visit with no complaints and the elephants were never bothered by us or any of the drivers.
