body: We visited the Hurulu Eco Park in April, which is when and where elephants are more likely to be spotted than in the other parks in the area. Three of us booked an inexpensive, private jeep tour, which lasted about 3 hours. It would have lasted longer, but we saw so many elephants, and so close to our jeep, in the first few hours that we were ready to go back to our hotel early. Not that there are hundreds of elephants thundering around at this time of year, but we saw 5 herds of 5-10 elephants each. At one point the elephants walked close enough that our driver had us move to the opposite side of the jeep and put it in gear to drive away, but the elephants were just munching away as they walked and didn’t display any aggression and we ended up staying put. So, full points for elephant viewing, even in the low season. The Eco-park is a large, undeveloped area and is not fenced off or anything, so there are true wild elephants who are just passing through the area as they roam around Sri Lanka. Initially, the word “eco” in the park name put me off because it sounded like greenwashing of a potentially dubious commercial enterprise, but it appears to be a legit, protected wildlife area. And very conveniently close to Habarana. In fact, you can sometimes see wild elephants from the highway that runs through town, much to the annoyance of local farmers. (The fact of the impinging elephants, not the fact of their visibility from the road.) Or sometimes elephants block the road, much to the delight of tourists and annoyance of local commuters.My only complaint about our Eco Park experience is that there were a ton of other jeeps driving around the dirt roads of the Eco Park. Sometimes this caused mini traffic jams. Sometimes it got loud with so many engines running. Sometimes jeeps disturbed elephants and caused them to walk away, back into the forest cover. When one jeep finds a herd, all the other jeeps come a-running over, causing quite a scene. Sometimes there were as many as 20 jeeps, engines loudly rumbling, in a tangled mass, sitting near a herd of elephants. But, we were part of the problem in our jeep, so I have no right to complain. And at times there were magical moments, when we were the only jeep in sight, and we happened upon a small herd, and we shut our engine off, and we enjoyed a close encounter for a good 10 minutes until the elephants moved on as they pulled up grass to eat.
title: Elephants good, crowds bad, result = average.

body: We visited the park,on an afternoon safari,saw a lot of elephants,verry close to our jeep also a lot of birds.There where not so manny jeeps in the parkAfter safari when we went by jeep back to Guesthouse,we saw also a lot of elephants along the main road

body: We would love to give this place no dots but sadly not possible. As other people have said this place is too overcrowded with vehicles when elephants are spotted. All jostling for position. At one time there was a herd on the track and the driver was wary of getting too close as they have been known to attack, so he kept a safe distance. But within 10 minutes there was a traffic jam of at least 25 vehicles all around, some got too close and were charged by one of the elephants. Others had circled round to the other side of the road and essentially pinned the herd in causing visible distress to the animals. Some vehicles ran the gauntlet past the elephants and were chased. And because they made it they were cheering. Don't think they would be cheering quite so much if this had caused the matriarch to attack the other vehicles. Which would have been easy as there were sp many jeeps around they would never have been able to get out of the way. I wish we had never gone on this trip and would not recommend it to anyone. Management may read this review but won't reply as it os so negative. Even if it was a positive one they just cut and paste the same pointless one.
title: Not good

body: Don't waste your money and insist on going to one of the official national parks. body: My group mainly are young people.. We all enjoyed the jeep riding and racing along the road. Then, after drove further at bumpy road, we saw a group of elephants... So near, We also managed to spot some birds and eagles.. We joined the afternoon ride.. The sun is very strong and also dusty. Do not forget to bring your hat that can be tied up and mask.. Apply your sun block.

body: We went on this safari at about 4pm and about one hour into the journey we saw loads of elephants. The only down side is that there are a lot of jeeps in the park at the same time and as soon as a herd of elephants is spotted they all charge to the one place which just seems a bit horrible. The car fumes were something else !. But saying that the elephants didn't seem bothered and just carried on regardless.

body: I've rated this experience as excellent, as I never thought I would get to see elephants so up close, however, there are areas in which how this is run could improve.We booked this safari not really knowing what to expect, it was suggested by the owner of our homestay. When we got there, there were at least another 6 jeeps, we paid the entrance fee and set off, when we were driving around initially it appeared as though each jeep took different routes, however, after about 30 minutes, one jeep saw some elephants and all the jeeps conglomerated around them, there must have been about 12 in total. On the positive, they all switched their engines off, to watch them in silence and the elephants were able to leave if they were not comfortable.On the negative side, the jeeps do appear to not care about the habitat once they have spotted the elephants, trampling through bushes to let their tourists get up close. There are also a number of tourists that were talking really loudly and did not appear to care about being quiet and disturbing the elephants (of course, inconsiderate tourists are not the park's fault and the drivers were attempting to ask them to be quiet)I think it would be better if they built a few viewing areas high up and the jeeps drove to these and tourists waited patiently, I would happily sit there for hours to get to see these beautiful creatures.
title: Elephants up close

body: Wonderful experience - a beautiful park and we saw lots of elephants up close and personal! Would recommend our guide Bertie.
title: Plenty of elephants!

body: We were prepared for disappointment after not seeing anything for the first half an hour, but our driver was confident and for the second half of the safari we lost count. After stopping and spending a good 15 minutes observing a family of elephants we toured the park 'spotting' elephants as we went. We lost count at 170! This place is by far teh best value park to visit for elephant safari.
title: Hundreds of Elephants!

body: Our jeep driver was great and showed us a beautiful park with plenty of wildlife. The main issue was the lack of regulation over numbers of jeeps - that other jeeps went off track damaging the habitat to get close to elephants.It felt very uncomfortable to see 5-6 jeeps doing this and elephants literally surrounded. Some mothers has calves and our driver explained that one mother who had a damaged ear had attacked his jeep and knocked a bumper off another. We watched 'back to back' jeeps unable to easily move away from an angry mother. We felt visitors' safety was therefore jeopardised.The situation would be so much better if restrictions were placed on jeep numbers and that drivers adhered to 20-30 metres/track only.We felt uncomfortable being part of this intrusion on the elephants and park, although thank goodness our driver kept to the tracks and agreed with us.Beautiful place but the Park authority should take a lot more care of the impact of increased tourism.
title: Park needs rules

body: Great way to see elephants in their on habitat. It was fun riding in an open Range Rover so that we could take pictures.
title: Elephant

body: We paid 14,000 LKR for a 3.5 hour jeep safari, arranged through our hotel.We saw approximately 60 elephants on the safari, although be warned that you can at times be driving around for ages without seeing any. We spent an hour driving round before we saw any. The park was great for seeing elephants, although not much other wildlife, although part of this might be down to the time we want (2.30 in the afternoon). It was brilliant seeing the elephants in their natural habitat, and although at times there can be a lot of jeeps, they stick to the tracks and don't encroach on the elephants' personal space. The guides have walkie talkies and will inform each other where the elephants are, which is good in that you don't miss out but sometimes a shame that you have to share the moment with others! Generally when you are on the tracks however you feel like you have the park to yourself.The jeep ride itself is quite fun as there are lots of bumpy tracks and you can stand up in the back of the truck.It is recommended that you check with your hotel which park has the most elephants in at any one time - depending on season, Minneriya and Kaudulla can be better.
title: Fantastic way to see the elephants in their natural habitat

body: Originally I was a bit sceptic when our host discouraged us from Minneriya and Kaudulla National Parks and sent us there, but then... families and groups of elephants, extremely close to our jeep yet still relaxedly grazing their way past... an unforgettable experience!We were told we were very lucky to see so many - in any case it was absolutely fascinating!!

body: The jeep drivers here do not seem to follow any rules. The advantage is that you get quite close to the elephants. However, we were disturbed by how they trample over pristine stands of grass habitat.
title: Great for close-up images of elephants

body: Simply brilliant way to see elephants in a truly natural environment, you get really close to them and the guides are very knowledgeable.
title: A wonderful way to see the elephants in a natural environment.

body: If you go to Habarana, Sigiriya, Dambulla area one thing you have to do is go for Elephants safari.It's Minneriya, Kaudulla or Eco Park.This time of the year it's Eco Park.Definitely you will see more than 50 elephants.Yes I have even more than 50.

body: We had planned to go to Minneriya to see elephants, but were advised by everyone that at this time of the season Hurulu was the place. It's a short distance north of Habarana. But we argued that the tourist interest maintains the value of the living herd. The landscape is wonderful to drive through - just a pity it was in a nose-to-tail crawling progression of vehicles. Was it worth it? Yes.
title: Gorgeous animals in a stunning landscape

body: We saw about twenty five elephants. Each time there were groups of four to five with a couple of solo male sightings as well. Twice we saw tiny baby elephants who mostly spent their time under their mothers torso. The amount of safari jeeps was kind of troubling - about twenty the afternoon we were there. However seeing the wild elephants was really great. At the end our guide detoured back into the jungle as the sun was setting for a very magical time. In addition to elephants we saw peacocks, hawk Eagles, parrots and other bird life.
title: Fun but a lot of jeeps

body: If you are used to seeing elephants in Africa, this will seem very different. These are jungle elephants and much harder to find and to see once you do find them. The foliage is dense and obstructs the views. Having said that, it is pretty special to see an elephant in the wild. Asian elephants have smaller ears and in Sri Lanka they are mostly tuskless due to killing off all the tuskers years ago. In this park, you drive around in a jeep looking for elephants. Once one or a few are found, the jeeps tend to converge so this is hardly a serene bonding experience. The guides are impressively good at finding them given the difficulty and positioning you so you can get a picture. They are also respectful of the animals and given them their space. We had a guide who was pretty good at birding and so we saw some cool birds while we were looking for the elephants. We subsequently saw elephants at Yala park and they were similarly hard to find and to see so I think the eco park is a good option if you are in the area. I think the nature of these elephants means that it will either be an artificial situation (elephant riding, domesticated elephants), or they will be hard to find and see. Another difference from African wildlife viewing is that because they are consumed by the jungle when they move away, you never get to see any behaviors. You get a glimpse and some pictures but it is very unusual to send enough time to observe behaviors. I would recommend this experience to anyone who wants to see elephants in the wild and doesn’t mind bumping around in a jeep for a couple of hours. I was glad I did it.
title: It is a good experience if your expectations are in line

body: Will be able to see closer to 15 elephants these days. There are few rock views, which will be great for someone who likes photography.
title: Safari at Eco Park

body: Far too many noisy and uncomfortable vehicles surrounding small elephant groups. We saw more from the main road that passes through the park. Frankly this place is a danger to wildlife.
title: Only OK for elephants

body: Great park with many elephants. Less expensive than other well known parks (Udawalawe and Yala). Lots of elephants has come to this area for climate reasons.
title: Many, many elephants!

body: We went on a safari late Feb. We were picked up at 15h30 and the reserve was a 10min drive from the Cinnamon Lodge. We then waited in the car park for 45mins whilst the driver queued for tickets which was annoying. We had read some other reviews and were wondering if this was a bad idea. Also we had been told that there were no elephants at Minneyria which I wasn't sure was correct. On the plus side all the other jeeps had gone in already so we were not crawling along. We immediately saw elephants and the jeeps were all getting very close and circling them. Not great. After that though we were mostly alone and in fact all the other wildlife and scenery was stunning enough. We saw Snake Eagles, Open billed Storks, Bee Eaters and loads more than I don't know. The roads are very bumpy but the 3 kids we were with loved every minute of the 2 and a half hours. At the end after sunset by the exit of the park we saw more elephants and since there were fewer jeeps it was much more of a magical experience and they came close to the stationary car. We paid 30$ for an adult and half for a kid ticket and I think it was good value.
title: Slightly worried at first but turned out to be excellent

body: If you want to see wild elephants, this is a great place. There are three parks in this region, and elephants may congregate in one or another - so some local knowledge here is really helpful when choosing which to visit. The tour was in open topped jeeps. The park has very long grass and lots of vegetation. You are likely to see big groups of elephants, but they may be quite obscured by long grass. The roads are well maintained (given where they are and the need to be unobtrusive. My group went straight in, none of the queueing mentioned by others - we went quite late in the day so maybe that's a good time to go. There were quite a few jeeps around and around the main groups of elephants, but I wouldn't go as far as calling it crowded, compared to other natural attractions worldwide. All of the jeeps that I saw were giving the animals a good distance and didn't obviously break any of the codes around safari operation.If you want to spot lots of different wildlife, there are national parks with more on offer. However if you want to just focus on elephants, this is a good place to come where you are likely to see plenty of animals.
title: Good opportunity to see lots of elephants

body: The title says it all. The guide we had was really good and the park was not to busy the other parks were flooded so this was probably a good time to visit this particular park and was only 20mons from the hotel.
title: Saw 50 elephants in three hours what more can I say!!

body: The park has very good offering to get close to elephants but its not well organised. You have to wait in a long queue to get entry tickets, Safari jeep drivers are behaving like crooks. All this makes, the experience stress full and unpleasant.All in all there are about 60 jeeps driving around in search of elephants which makes it a noisy spot.

body: Long wait at the gate.Short safari about 02 hrs.Only elephants and few birds were there. internal roads were not properly maintained.Nice lookout which is on top of a huge rock gives a 360 degree view .

body: We loved our afternoon seeing the elephants. It was a little strange seeing so many jeeps there so it is nice when you are alone rather than in a long line. body: Thus place is good for only those for whom elephants are new. Apart from elephants there are hardly any species available.

body: We had a very close encounter with a heard of wild elephants here, and saw a lot of other wild life. Another must visit sites and I definitely will go again

body: To be fair, we did see lots of elephants but also lots of trucks with people holding loud conversations with each other. The drivers are aggressive at getting you the best view so go off-road in seriously bumpy places!

body: Our plan was to do Minneriya National Park, but since it was flooded our hotel recommended this park instead. Less jeeps any felt much more authentic - not like a zoo (as it felt like driving around in Yala and Udawalawe).
title: Lots of elephants!!!

body: Tour guides somewhat wild. The roads have large potholes and many areas where it is flooded so be prepared for that. The guides do go out of their way to show you elephants. title: Elephant safari

body: I have never been so close to an elephant in the wild before. Really exciting. Saw c30 over the 3 hour safari.
title: Best Elephant Sightings

body: We were told that Minneriya was flooded and the elephants were in Eco Park. We weren't quite sure, but took the tour. First it was disappointing as no elephants visible at all, but then on the way back already to exit we saw suddenly plenty of elephants from quite close. We saw more elephants crossing the road on the way back to Habarana. As always lots of jeeps around with tourists, all wanting to see the elephants and crowding around every sighting.
title: Positive surprise

body: Fantastic park full of Elephants! Fun safari through the park. We saw between 20-30 elephants, including a baby with mother, feeding within 4 feet of us! Incredible!
title: Elephants in the wild!

body: We visited Hurulu because of flooding in Minneriya and we caught an interesting sighting of a family of elephants walking single file through the scrubland ... but not a lot else.
title: Limited sightings

body: Then this is the place to go: you drive along a circular loop almost in a convoy of jeeps. Some of the drivers have no respect at all for the elefants and try to get as close as possible. With this they also kill the rest of the fauna and flora of the park. Besides the 10 to 15 elephants, we bearly saw birds or reptiles. We went with the nature guide of the "Rice Villa". He luckily did respect the elephants!
title: You want to see how elephants are chased by jeeps?

body: We visited this park as an organised trip via our private tour (Trailfineders UK). Walkers tours were the agent responsible for our in country trips. I can only say that we had the most brilliant of guide CHANDRASIRI. We were already staying in Habarana so it didn't take long to get to Echo Park unlike some of the other reviewers. Once at the park we entered immediately and CHANDRASIRI is clearly elephant man as he knew exactly where to drive to find the elephants, we saw very many and managed to get up extremely close. We were in a Jeep and part of the experience was made by the at times 'rough roads' which may not be everyone's cup of tea. Nothing was too much for our guide. Thoroughly enjoyed it. On our way out we did pass many other jeeps doing the trip, clearly many had been having difficulty finding elephants but our guide did give them directions. It did look like a convoy of vehicles all going the same way and if we had been part of that we probably would not have enjoyed it the same. Tips 1) book well and choose CHANDRASIRI and walkers tours, they are brilliant. 2) If you don't like being jostled around in a jeep it's not for you 3) ladies wear shorts rather than a dress or skirt 4) Don't make a lot of noise it will startle them 5) Hold on tight!!!!! If you are concerned about elephant welfare be reassured that on our tour at least, we saw them to be happy with vehicle/human proximity
title: Excellent guide made this experience

body: Really not our thing. Far too many jeeps. Terrible road which seemed to just run from one end to the other (we didn't double back). Barely saw an elephant and if there was one, totally overrun with jeeps and noisy people. Waste of money. Def wouldn't recommend. Maybe worse because Minneriya apparently was not open.
title: Jamboree of Jeeps

body: Due to rain in the past few days, all the elephants had to go higher ground so our driver recommended this park instead. It was great fun as we got to see so many elephants including baby ones.
title: Good alternative to Minneriya National Park

body: We visited mid afternoon with a driver and jeep arranged through our accommodation (jeep and driver £15).Entry to the park us £5 per vehicle and £5 per person.We were quickly followed by a couple more jeeps forming a bit of a convoy.After about 15 minutes we saw a number of jeeps stationary up ahead, so our convoy headed over. On arrival there was a small group of elephants feeding.There was plenty of jockying fir position amongst the jeeps, although the elephants didn't appear to be concerned.After the photo opportunity we set off again and were soon alone on the jungle tracks. These were very bumpy, and it was more comfortable to stand with your head of the open top.In fact travelling like this was an enjoyable experience in itself, and I wouldn't have been too disappointed if we hadn't seen any elephants.Some time later we joined a gaggle of jeeps that had closed in on a small group of elephants. The same happened later again, although our driver took a different route and we came face to face with a marvellous elephant.The entire tour took about 2 and a half hours and was a really enjoyable way to spend an afternoon for any tourist based in the cultural triangle.
title: Very enjoyable

body: we originally wanted to go to Minneriya national park but we were told it was closed due to flooding. (and while on the road, we could indeed see a lot of areas were flooded due to heavy rain, we actually had a lot of rain in Dec which we were told is very odd because usually Dec is high season and dry) Supposedly the elephants also moved due to flooding and thats why I think Eco park had lots of elephants. There were wild elephants everywhere very close, even crossing the roads the safari jeeps were on. (unlike Yala, where we saw 1 elepant in the distance) It was a joy to watch the several elephant families. We went in the afternoon and there werent as many jeeps. at one point we were alone even. This was a great experience and much better than eg pinawalla orphanage where you sometimes feel sorry for the chained elephants.
title: beautiful

body: The park officials allow 10 -12 vehicles into the park all at once at 4 pm. The first vehicle spots an elephant and stays there for over 20 minutes. The vehicles at the back do not get an opportunity to see any animals. Every time the first vehicle spotted an elephant all the other vehicles were stuck behind this vehicle unable to move anywhere. Do not go on this safari. Waste of time and money
title: Elephant Safari

body: Finally we were lucky that we saw wild elephants. The park is pretty much crowded with Jeeps all searching for wildlife.
title: Jeeps and Elephants

body: Had a great experience with our driver, he seemed experienced and knew what he was was doing. Eco park was quite busy with many other jeeps but things seemed to move quite smoothly Rain kept pouring down throughout which we thought added to the experience! Heaps of elephants, peacocks, deer and various other birds The four wheel driving was also heaps of funWould definitely recommend this activity for those that enjoy the outdoors and wildlife
title: Really good

body: The tour company booked this Safari to ECO park. It rained on us but that is ok there is a trap to cover the seat in the back. Once we saw the wild elephants ir really didn't make any diffeance to us. We saw peacoks in park. Hearing the bull elephant call out to the females was wonderful to hear in the wild. The female elephant called back. We saw the many elephants and peacoks in area, Our driver was good at lcoatring the animals and birds.
title: 15 days in Sri Lanka

body: after driving around for quite a while on a peacock safari we at last came across about 10 elephants that were amazing. unfortunately the drivers do all drive in as close as possible to the elephants which of course gives a great view but feels so wrong intruding on the elephants especially the babies - but we were very lucky to see them.
title: awesome elephants

body: We went in with a Jeep we organized through a Tukutuk driver (all very friendly, we didn't feel like they were trying to rip us off, also the price was better than what the hotel offered), entrance was included in the Jeep rental. Went on over bumpy dirt roads for a while, you get the real Safari feeling on the back of the vehicle all bouncing around, great fun. Deep in the area we finally saw a whole bunch of elephants in different groups, even a baby. It was amazing, totally recommend. And big plus: not many people even in the high season.
title: Great experience

body: We wanted to visit a national park and see some elephants. We had a driver for our trip in northern Sri Lanka and he said he would arrange this for us. He got us a jeep and took us here because the other parks were "flooded". This is a routine scam. We were staying at a home stay nearby and our hosts helped us research the prices and park by calling trusted friends. This park is NOT a national park. The cost is half the price or less of the national parks. You should not be paying 40 dollars a person! The cost is NOT 5,000 rupees. The national park is not flooded, this is just the lie to get you here. The drivers and guides are pocketing the double fee. We confronted our guide and managed to get half of our money back after a huge debate. He admitted the scam to us after we called him out. We did see elephants in the park, as well as a peacock, mongooses and a hawk. But the park has tall grass making it quite difficult to see the animals.There are no bodies of water. From pictures and reports from other people, there are much nicer parks in the area with less obstructing the views. Be wary if you want to visit here. Stop at the entrance and buy the ticket yourself and get a receipt.
title: Park Ok but Tourists are Scammed Here!!!!

body: It was a rainy day so I believe there was a lot less jeeps there than usual. I hired a jeep to myself and was rewarded with a peaceful drive until we caught up with the others. We saw about 20 elephants and one shy peacock. It was entertaining, but the best part of this safari was when it ended and we were driving back to the hotel. In between two national parks u can see elephants crossing the road. This is what happened around 5.30 in evening. The ma and pa were protecting a baby elephant and it was adorable having such s close view. They crossed and the pa decided that one car was too close and started an intimidation tactic, running towards it temper flaring. My driver reacted quickly and moved incase it went for us. I had also seen elephants on road side the day before. If u don't want to pay the money for a safari then just drive the route between the national parks and u will likely see some between 5-6 pm.
title: Was enjoyable but not a must

body: If you are looking for anything but elephant, you will probably be disappointed. The safari is like bumper to bumper traffic in Colombo, for most parts, with all the operators going in at the same entrance and "hunting" for the sightings on the same roads. The experience was decent enough, especially for someone like me who just likes being outdoors in the wild. We did see two sightings of elephant, so it was mission accomplished.
title: Elephant Safari

body: Went here because minneriya was closed due to rains flooding the park. We went in around 12 noon, not the most ideal time. But the weather was gloomy and we had a bit of rain. So it was ok for elephant viewing. Elephants were pretty docile so hung around for some time around the Safari trucks. On the way back got to see more elephants on the trinco main road as well. This area has a lot of elephants, so it's always a good area to see them.
title: Plenty of elephants

body: We visited here in December as part of an organised tour. The elephants had migrated into the eco park areas as the other local national parks had flooded. We had a fantastic experience getting very close to the elephants. We saw at least 30 including younger ones too! We also saw lots of tropical birds and eagles. Our driver Tommy was great - very friendly and knowledgable on the animals we saw. Would recommend for an elephant safari! Obviously it depends on where the elephants are that day in the surrounding areas as to how many you will see on your trip.
title: Enjoyable elephant extravaganza

body: Wow! We were hardly lucky to spot any wild animals in the many wild safaris in the sub-continent. This was a real deal. Within 5 minutes from the start we got to see an adolescent solitary elephant with small tusks emerging. Within the next 10 minutes we saw a herd of about 10 grazing amidst the tall grasses. Our driver displayed his 4-wheel driving skills and got really close to the herd. But the grass was still quite tall to reveal the elephants completely. We saw 2 more such herds in different spots. We got to see some peacocks/peahen and an eagle perched on a very tall tree. No sightings of deer, monkeys or leopards can be expected to be seen in this parkThe highlight was towards the end when we were on the way to the exit. A pregnant mother with 2 calves of different ages and a young adult appeared from nowhere. There about 4 jeeps and all the tourists were thoroughly excited to see this small herd only about 15 feet away. That was real up close and felt our trip was already rewarding.
title: Got to see a lot of wild elephant herds

body: It's a very nice site for wandering and checking nature, not too many animals, just a few elephants, and we saw a peacock far away. It's nice as much as you don't expect too many animals.
title: Not a bad site

body: It was a great blasting experience Any sight seer should never miss this wonderful Elephant paradise
title: Safari to Eco Park

body: We were staying three nights in Habarana to do two things: we wanted to visit Sigiriya and we also wanted to visit Kudulla national park. We let our hotel manager know that we wanted to visit Kadulla and he said he would arrange it for 5000LKR for the two of us. The next day he told us that he's spoken to some friends and that Kadulla was flooded and instead we should go to Hurulu Eco Park. We said we'd look into it but after research we weren't interested - especially as it wasn't in our guide book nor had there been a review of the park on tripadvisor for several months. However, on the day of the trip we felt very pressured by the hotel manager, the driver and the guide to go to this park and, sadly, caved as we thought they might know the best. To be fair we DID see elephants, BUT it wasn't what we expected. Kadulla is supposed to have hundreds of elephants and we saw about 30 tops. The ones we did see where very hard to actually see as the grass is almost as high as the elephants and cover them completely. While Kadulla reportedly had massive herds which are visible on the clear plains, we really struggled to see the elephants and the largest group we saw was 8. On top of this the track is very very very bumpy so was quite an uncomfortable ride. Of course we don't know if maybe Kadulla was really flooded, but visiting this park wasn't our original plan and I regret not sticking to our guns and seeing for ourselves. I guess it depends what you want to get out of your safari trip. As we had previously visited some other parks (Uda Walawe and Yala) we were hoping for the massive, clearly visible herds that Kadulla promised. Overall, we did see elephants, but just left feeling a little let down and we really felt we were pressured into doing something we didn't want to do. (Went on safari trip on the 5th of December, 5,000LKR for 2 people minus the entry fee, 3 1/2 hour trip.)
title: Just don't do it unless you actually want to

body: This trip was exactly what was promised a safari where we got to see lots of wild elephants. The trip was a bit expensive at USD 50 per person, but we were treated very professionaly and our driver was very informative and a great guide. We saw many groups of elephants including several young elephants. There were also some exotic birds (hawks and parrots) and the park itself was nice. It was a very pleasant afternoon and took around 3 hours. Would recommend for family groups as well.
title: If you like elephants...

body: This is so easy access from Habarana junction an the park along the highway. Entrance cost also quite cheaper than Minneriya and Kaudula specially for foreign visitors. in the wet season Minneriya and Kaudula lakes water level has increased so most wild elephants moves to this forest block but this cant compare for that view. so many small elephants groups through the bushes an some times get close and cross the track.
title: The only seasonal option instead for Minneriya - By Serendib Traveller

body: Hurulu Eco Park is ideal place to see wild elephants but honestly we can see elephants in this park is only from February to end of May or big in in or June. Here You can see Elephants as small herd but you can see in minneriya as large group but minneriya is ideal only July onward.This hurulu park was named as protected nature reserve by Government in 1977 and it located 150 above sea level in dry zone of Habarana.
title: Ideal spot for elephant in February to May.

body: Took an afternoon safari jeep ride and was quite a amazed to see at least 50 elephants including several young ones with mothers. Several were seen really close up including one crossing the main road to join it's family group casually grazing very close to the road edge.There were many in the surrounding areas. Taken by my driver I was picked up from the Rukmali Hotel in an open top jeep I had a great 3 1/2 hours. The Park costs 1350 rps and the driver asked for 3500 for his hire ( plus tip 500 ) he wouldn't give me a written receipt so not sure if I was ripped off here.
title: Saw 50 elephants

body: There are two other popular reserve/parks - Minneriya and Kaudulla. Those have variety of animals. Hurulu has mainly elephants and the occasional birds. That may be good news if you want to guaranteed sighting of many elephants. We saw plenty of them up-close - including many baby elephants. There are many tourist / jeep operators. Most charge a flat fee of 35 USD / per person (includes jeep, entrace tickets etc.)I would recommend you make a trip. There are jeeps available for hire right outside Chaaya Village/Cinnamon Lodge. The prices quotes by the hotel will likely be a bit higher. You should just head out to the main road and try bargaining.
title: The 3rd choice - that many may not opt / know ...

body: We were a group of 12 with ages ranging from 5 to 79. We stayed at Hotel Sigiriya and the safari was arranged by the hotel. The two safari jeeps picked us up from the hotel, a 1/2 hr drive later we were at the entrance to the Eco Park.Prices were reasonable with half price for children under 12. Funnily we were asked to show the kids' passports to prove their ages!Our safari driver was excellent, he spotted an elephant hidden among the rocks on a hill at least a kilometer away, we took the longest time to spot it ourselves. I managed to photograph it on a 300mm lens and it appears small and well camouflaged, and the fact that he was able to spot it at such a distance while driving the jeep in 7ft high grass still boggles my mind. We sighted 3 large families of elephants with their young at close range. An amazing experience to watch these gentle giants go about their dinner with little ones frolicking about!Although we weren't too close by one adult decided she'd had enough of us and decided to charge! With much ear flapping, trumpeting and ground stomping, it was a terrifying experience (definitely for one septuagenarian in our group).Overall, a bone jarring drive, sighting elephants in their natural environment, well worth the money.
title: Elephants! And a fantastic safari driver

body: We are animal lovers, particularly, for elephants and we saw quite a few including the young. Birds were also seen but if you are looking for other wildlife there is not alot or we did not see alot.
title: Elephants

body: Very good jungle to go and visit handle of elephants , good experience to go mud road and terrain , Bala fffdffg. Fghhhhh. Gjbhnnnmnmbhjj
title: GM

body: We had a young but very professional driver. Smooth driving. He was very good in reading the way of elephants. We were very lucky to meet and see a group of elephants very close. But driver was also looking for birds. Client satisfaction is high ranked.
title: Lucky to see elephants very close

body: Went for a jungle safari during our SL visit with our 2 children (5yo & 2yo) and they thoroughly enjoyed it. there were elephants and eagles (don't expect much more though). Was very fascinating to see their growing family as in most other places, you'd only see adult elephants. thoroughly enjoyed it. Extremely comfy jeep and the driver was amazing too. he had cold bottles of water as well as fruit platter waiting for us when we finished our trek up a rock. Though its not a place to review the organizer, Fernando adventure safari, +94 77 364 8653 organised everything for us. All in all an extremely good visit.
title: Elephants and eagles

body: The wild elephant safari at this park was very good,only problem it was overcrowded with many safari jeeps ,and the tourists were very noisy the tour guide should brief them before not to make a noise we were able to see many elephants
title: wild elephant safari

body: Like previous reviewers, we were a little dubious after being told that there were no elephants at Minneriya during April when trying to organise a safari but they could be found at the "Eco Park". After a bit of research and based on previous reviews, we decided to go to Minneriya first (no elephants) so we visited Hurulu the next day.While there were plenty of elephants and the park itself is quite pretty, there were far too many jeeps and I felt that they got too close to the elephants. The elephants didn't seem particularly bothered, but I think the park needs some more regulation.Definitely great for elephant spotting, but you will get the feeling of being in a zoo. Best to go during the afternoon, the total tour time is around 3.5 hours.
title: Great elephant spotting, but a bit zoo-like

body: It is a beautiful park, with lush greenery (and breathtaking landscapes from the viewing point). We saw many elephants, from very close, including a few extremely cute babies being protected by their parents.It is a shame that some jeep drivers are ready to frighten the elephants by getting very close for a few quick photos for the tourists.This is a good option if, as in our case, you cannot visit Minneriya National park because of excessive rain. We booked with the Grand Meaulnes Family hotel. The jeep cost 4000 rupees and then entry to the park was 1000 per person +tax +vehicle fee +driver fee.
title: Elephants a plenty and SO CLOSE!

body: We were lucky to see several groups of elephant including a mother with a two-week old baby. I am concerned that too many jeeps pursuing elephants like paparazzi will have a negative impact on their welfare.
title: Baby elephant

body: We hired a jeep and driver to spend the afternoon in this reserve and enjoyed seeing lots of wild elephants plus other interesting wildlife.
title: great place to see wild elephants

body: We went on a 2 hour tour and were very lucky to see lots of elephants. Our driver got us very close so we had an excellent view. It was a bit scary when one looked like it was going to charge though! Luckily it didn't, but our guide assured us that the jeeps are very strong (much safer in them than out!)
title: Excellent elephant experience!

body: For 50$ per person, we had a nice 3-hour elephant safari in this medium-sized reserve. Although, at some points the jeep density was higher than the elephant density.
title: Elephants in the wild

body: At first was a little disappointed that it was the wrong season to visit Minneriya but was happily surprised we saw a number of elephants at Hurulu Eco Park. First 45min was a bit slow but we saw more and more as the tour went on. Be prepared for a bumpy ride. We felt a couple of jeep drivers got a bit close to the elephants and scared them off but mostly the drivers were fairly courteous to the animals. Viewing platform was a welcome break to get out of the jeep, stretch the legs up the hill and see a few more elephants grazing in the distance. 2.5-3 hour tour ended with us seeing a herd of about 10 elephants (including some baby ones!) grazing alongside the road on the way home. Bonus!
title: Great first time safari

body: Seeing the baby elephants really was a highlight of our trip - fabulous place although a little over run with jeeps - worth a visit!
title: Elephants galore!!

body: This Eco Park was apoarently only created in February 2008 and civers some 10000 hectares.It is within 150 metres of Harbarana railway station served by the excellent and enjoyable Sri Lankan Railways trains. Our special train had dropped us off earlier as we toured Sigiriya Rock but we later returned by our ciach following the train around to tour the Eco Park.I did not directly pay the admission fees but I assume that as is sadly typical of Sri Lanka, foreigners are charged more than locals, a discriminatiry practice nit often oractised in other nations.The Eco Park offers jeep safaris. Most vehicles have longitudinal seating for six. A few have transverse seating that may be more comfortable.On our 163 minute excursion we saw at least 25 elephants including a herd. The waterways are narrow so larger herds cannot bathe together.There were six jeeps in our group but at the viewing platform rock just prior to the tour's end there were as many as 19 vehicles.While this led to some questionable practices such as going off the dirt tracks to get closer photos of the elephants or almost surrounding a few elephants with a group of motor vehicles full if excited foreigners, on balance this is preferable to the elephants being chained as is true for some at the very commercial so called elephant orphanage or shot by poachers. Yes, some flora may be destiryed by the jeeps but they do not go into every area of this reserve.Whether or not the drivers were trying to provoke the elephants to charge is an unknown to me, but at the end of the trip the drivers supposedly expect a Rp200 tip although when some gave kess, they did not complain. It is true however that Africa may offer a more genuine experience covering much larger areas but not everyone has the time, money or oerceptions of safety to travel to South Africa or Zimbabwe.We returned via the main road to the starting point.Overall it was enjoyable including watching the occasional baby elephant.Older visitors could travel at one per jeep next to the driver as you have to climb into the back of the jeep.
title: Close to railway station and a great wet season experience

body: We went on a drive in this park during the wet season and this was spectacular 4x4 driving by our driver. We also enjoyed the views and different, mostly elephants, in the park. Not quit as good as yala NP, as this is busier and more commercial, more tourists. However still enjoyable for an afternoon drive.
title: Spectacular drive during wet season

body: I was shocked at the number of vehicles here and that they are allowed to go off the designated tracks churning up habitat to get closer to the elephants i.e. To stress them out. At one point there were 19 jeeps encircling a small herd within a radius of about 25m, one drove within metres of a mother and calf. Most had engines running belching out carbon monoxide and toxic fumes,not just bad for the elephants but all the fauna and flora. Needs to be better managed.
title: If you love wildlife don't go

body: Very close encounters with a large group of elephants (30+), including several young ones. Didn't like the "scrum" of around 25 safari jeeps all jockeying for position with absolutely no regard for the animals with the result that one or two elephants became more aggressive. When we told our driver to withdraw and position our vehicle away from the scrum we got much better pictures as the elephants eventually came past us with no other vehicles to disturb them.
title: Great bird life and elephants.

body: Two hours to find a few elephants and ten other jeeps with no respect for the animals at all. Saw better sightings off the main road. If you want to see elephants go to Africa.
title: Go somewhere else

body: Smaller and cheaper than the other parks but so many beautiful wild elephants. I disagree with some reviews and felt that the drivers were very respectful of the animals and never felt like they were being harassed or scared. Our driver knew the park well and we were alone for a majority of the safari, however we did not use a driver from the park.
title: Beautiful elephants!

body: lots of elephants and birds. lots of jeeps too, its a shame they really disturbed the elephants.they enclosed the elephants from all sides. you can see they were frightend. the matriarch of the group became agresive.the nature iin the park is also worth looking at.the other 2 parks in the neighbour hood were closed because of the flooding, so ithey all came to this park.
title: lots of elephants

body: We went for a 2 hour evening drive in this national park and we got to see about 50 elephants. Though the terrain was rough, the driver / guide was fabulous in negotiating the terrain as well as getting the vehicle into right position for photography.
title: Elephant Park

body: This park is excellent for elephant safaris. Book them in Habarana (ensure you get on a Jeep with proper tires, the roads can be very bad). The park starts about a mile outside the village, and appeared to be full of elephants when we were there!
title: Elephants galore

body: This is a nice park to see elephants. However, we have been to other Sri Lankan parks and I think this is the least organized. Safari jeep drivers drive like crazy there, through bushes and grassland, destroying fragile ecosystem to bring you closer to the elephants. Although we were able to see elephants on a main road, I have a bad after taste from reckless driving there.
title: Elephants can be seen on the main road

body: Liked that we saw about 15 elephants with their young, but as soon as you saw something suddenly about another 20 jeeps arrived - made it feel like we were chasing them! Driver was delightful and they pickup and dropoff at Cinnamon Lodge.
title: Good side trip

body: This was supposed to be a sanctuary for wild elephants, instead what there was was a herd of elephants being chased around by a dozen off-the-road 4x4s. Hardly a sanctuary, these elephants were being tormented by the whole experience. It was little wonder that some of the males got very angry and threatened to charge us which if they had done so they could have easily overturned our jeep killing us.The problem is that these sort of places are huge tourist attractions for which huge pricces are chrged. As money-spinners in the end its the elephants which suffer the most. They should simply be left alone to roam the wild undisturbed.
title: Tortmented Elephants

body: Amazing place.. wonderful wildlife. We saw Alot of elephants and eagles. You should do jeep safari specially during raining.I recommended
title: Amazing park

body: Go here when the wet season has started, loads of elephants with young at very close range. Different experience from the other parks but as just as worthwhile.
title: Great park

body: Park is neighboring to Minneriya and Kaudulla National Parks,This is smaller park when comparing to other 2 parks of Minneriya and Kaudulla. As elephants moving from one park to other and for some months in the year, you can see elephants only in Hurulu Eco Park and that time no elephants in Minneriya or Kaudulla.This park is less expensive when compared to other national parks.So, better recommended to check with your safari jeep driver whether elephants available in the park before going to the park.Better you have 4WD jeep for this park.
title: Very nice jeep safari with off-road experience

body: Nobody should visit Sri Lanka without going to see wild Asian elephants. During the dry season Minneriya and Kaudulla are great to see lots of elephants. However, during the wet season, when the reservoirs are full, Hurulu Eco Park is a good alternative. You won't see as many elephants as in the other parks, but most likely you will see some. And seeing a wild elephant is always very special! You can go early morning or in the afternoon. No need to spend the whole day. Take water and snacks with you. Arrange for a local safari jeep to pick you up at your hotel. Tell the jeep driver that you want to stay on the roads and don't need to be too close to the elephants (some drivers seriously believe that they get better tips if they put the tourists right next to the elephants, which of course disturbs the animals).
title: Great to see elephants during the wet season

body: Be sure to get more than one offer and negotiate a better price!! For example, ask your hotel, and a driver or tour operator, and call the park directly, then negotiate.We were substantially overcharged! We only realized it, because when we arrived at the park, a couple wanted to just pay us to ride in our jeep, since we had plenty of space. However, when we mentioned our price, they found that they were already being offered a price that was less than half of that for their own private jeep! The price should be per jeep, not per person. The best price I have seen on here is 3500 rupees. Even with the higher price, it was an excellent excursion!This is one of the "Habarana parks"...the 3 parks (Minneriya, Kaudulla, Hurulu Ecopark) are somehow connected, same park rangers and guides or something. They then take you to whichever one where you are likely to see the most, depending on season, migration, flooding, etc. So, we were in Hurulu Ecopark and saw mostly elephants, some deer, water buffalo, monkeys, a few large eagles. I do not think there are leopards in this park. Yala is supposedly best for leopards, but that park is in the south and it depends on the time of year you visit.The elephants were great! At first, we saw just one walking and eating in the tall grass. Then, she was followed by her entire herd, including a relatively young, small elephant. They crossed the road directly in front of us and almost "posed" for photos. That was only the beginning.After a little driving around, we came upon two more herds and watched them for a long time. One aggressive female did not like us parked near her family, so she chased us away! She only ran a few meters behind us to chase the jeep away, but that is all it takes earn your respect! The other herd included several younger elephants and a baby born in this year. It was fascinating to just watch them, and of course take hundreds of photos. Then again, as the herd migrated in our direction, a very old female did not like our presence, and she trumpeted and charged a few steps in our direction. Again, that was more than enough to make our driver keep his distance.
title: Chased by elephants!

body: Many people are not aware of the Hurulu National Park or the Eco Park since it's being overshadowed by the adjoining Minneriya National Park. Hurulu is one of the 4 sites of the UNESCO Man & Biosphere Program. During our journey we thoroughly enjoyed the ride since many jeeps were not there. We saw the occasional jeep or two, but it was a refreshing ride to have a very silent park for wildlife photography. Our lenses caught many elephants, as well as spotted deer. We saw a deer carcass which confirmed the presence of the leopard in the park, which can almost be never seen. The big game drive included a short drive on the main road which was exquisite. This is another hot spot for elephants in Sri Lanka. Also the jeep hire charge is much less here compared to the Minneriya charges.
title: A nice getaway

body: Our driver arranged a jeep with a contact of his (3500rp for 2 of us) which seems pretty cheap compared to other reviews. We paid the park entrance separately and the park's spotter joined us. We went in the early morning (setting off at 6am from the hotel just down the road and were back at the hotel before 9am). Our driver recommended this park because the elephants at Minneriya National Park are apparently scattered at this time of year because the tanks (reservoirs) are full. The driver followed what seemed to be a set route around the park which was pretty bumpy. We detoured a few times in search of elephants and saw a group of about 7 or 8 feeding in the trees. Apparently the evening time is better as the elephants gather in an open area and during the day, the elephants go in search of shade.
title: Saw some wild elephants

body: This part is located near to hotel that we stayed, thus we took a private jeep next to our hotel and cost was 8000/- for eight of us!nevertheless for foreigners the cost may be higher than locals.once you enter the hirulu Eco Park! you have to take a entrance ticket for each and everyone (somewhere around 100/-). we entered to the park at 15:30 and left 18:15 so we have spend almost 2.5-3 hours !as an advice take litter of water per person at least else end of the the day you will be dehydrated and dead tiredit is a great and memorable elephant safari!
title: Bumpy jumpy Elephant Safari

body: We have just returned from a very enjoyable Elephant Safari, well worth the effort. Luckily after a slowish start we managed to see several groups of elephants including a few babies. Lots of interesting birds as well. The terrain is bumpy but probably to be expected, just take water and make sure to put on the sunscreen. Enjoy
title: Something Different

body: We took a private jeep tour to see the elephants in Hurulu. Cost was Rs 15,000 for three of us but that gave us a private jeep, driver and spotter. Tour lasted 2.5 hours which was about the right amount of time and included a stop with delicious fresh pineapple. We had a great trip and did see 6 or 7 groups of elephants plus numerous birds and other wildlife. It's fabulous to see these magnificent animals truly in the wild rather than chained up.The tracks are bumpy but that all adds to the experience and whilst there were other jeeps in the park, it didn't feel overly crowded. A really good late afternoon experience.
title: Worth a visit

body: This is small park, but to go thru it it will take cca 3 hours. We were lucky and see plenty of animals. We have seen from Elephant, lizards, falcon to wild peacocks and water buffalos. Definitely worth a visit. Take cap and water with you, sun is really brutal there.
title: very nice experience

body: Hurulu Biosphere Eco Park near DambullaJeep safaris through the Hurulu Eco Park are becoming ever more popular. A number of private companies provide four/five hour safaris, either during morning or afternoon.I chose to book one which would end when the sun was low in the sky, when shadows and soft light are perfect for photography.So at 2pm I boarded an open-top pick-up truck and off we went into the scrubland and virtually untouched wilderness to be found a few miles away from Habarana in central Sri Lanka.Not for the faint hearted or persons unprepared for the bumpiest ride of their lives...but...for the opportunity to get up close and personal with family groups of wild elephant, a few backside bruises is a small price to pay.The guides/drivers on all these vehicles are well versed as to what their clients expect to see and make every effort to fulfil those desires. As for me, the hours went by unnoticed as the viewfinders of my camcorder and Nikon SLR were alternately, pressed to my eye.At such close distances, the elephants are indeed majestic animals. Family groups stick close together, the babies flapping their undeveloped trunks at anything and everything...but constantly protected by their elders and prevented from wandering by delicate nudges of foot or trunk. It's a joy to behold.From the safety of the pick-up...after being driven to a spot considered 'near enough' by guides, the antics (and smells) of the herd can be savoured (sorry for the pun!) Under no circumstances are those on tour allowed to leave their vehicles. Elephants have become somewhat tolerant of vehicles in their vicinity but are extremely nervous when seeing or smelling a human on foot. They will indeed charge with ferocious force, should they feel threatened in any way by anyone being so foolish as to dismount. So folks, stay put, look, see and leave it at that.For the price paid the entire experience has few parallels. Not the Serengeti by any means but worth every penny.
title: Humps, bumps and trunks

body: i enjoyed my trip to the park very much concerning all the animals I could see. elephants, many, many elephants! BUT: The responsible staff should work on not sending 1 or 2 people per jeep into the park but join the groups. That would have the effect that less jeeps would cruise around and sort of chase the animals. Cause the way it is done now: Not very eco in my opinion.. In addition to that I saw people throwing litter from the jeeps into the park. The staff should inform visitors by entering the park that this is strictly forbidden! Still: the safari is worth it. Wonderful!
title: Fantastic elephant-watch but lack of "Eco"

body: Stayed in Dambulla and wanted to go to Kaudulla or Minneriya. Our hotel (Sundaras) receptionist told us that at the moment all the elephants were in the "Eco park". I was initially sceptical as I thought this might be a typical Sri lankan trick of getting tourists to visit somewhere their friends work, etc. but after checking online it sounded alright, so we went for it.Price was a lot cheaper than the other national parks (~3000 rupees to get in, including guide), and we did see a LOT of elephants - one protective Daddy elephant even charged our car, which was pretty terrifying but makes for a good story I suppose.The big downside for me was the bumpy terrain - the roads inside the park are very poor and I have bruises from being thrown about in the Jeep. However other people didn't seem to be having this problem.On the plus side, the scenery is amazing and the guides are good at spotting animals to show.
title: Lots of elephants, bumpy terrain

body: We went there because recent rains meant the elephants had deserted the parts of the Minneriya National Park which we would have otherwise visited. Be prepared for some very uneven roads but you should see lots of elephants very close up (but not much else!)
title: Masses of elephants

body: Minneryia, where we had previously had a memorable trip to see elephants some years ago, was too full of water so the hotel recommend this area instead. And we certainly saw many elephants of all sizes - and butterflies the size of dinner plates and birds walking on lotus lily pads and termite hills and weird rock formations and lush vegetation. Jeep wonderfully battered, roadways churned to Devon red mud - all great fun. And from the road on the way back to Giritale we saw more elephants, monkeys and deer - a memorable trip .
title: Elephants and more

body: Jeeps a tad uncomfortable as roads very bad but we saw a wonderful amount of elephants. All shapes and sizes, driving off the paths could often get quite close. About 20 jeeps the day we went but we were near the front so saw lots even on the main roadside heading back to our starting place.
title: Elephants

body: A jeep safari to Hurulu Eco park is a must if you are staying in Habarana - we travelled in a jeep from Hasthi Restaurant (a good place to eat too!)
title: Elephants galore in a natural environment

body: Eco Park is the best alternative for Minneriya National Park.When ever Minneriya is not accessible due to heavy rain one can take the safari at the Eco Park.The advantage in Eco park is that one could see some elephants for sure with in a shorter distance.I have heard that some one saw a leopard or a wild cat while their jeep broke down.I guess the roads must be done & the network of roads must extend beyond the present limits.
title: Eco Park - Worth For Money

body: Great place to spot elephants. During our 2 hour safari, we saw over 40 elephants, eagles and peacocks..
title: Great Elephant spotting and birds

body: Very nice park, with a lot of elephant families very easy to spot. Great driving in the rain and mud !!! One of the highlights of the trip
title: Great safari

body: Don't let the name mislead you - there is nothing particularly ecologically friendly about Eco Park. There had been a lot of rain the day before and as a result several tracks were impassable. There are a straggle of different drivers with varying skill in maneuvering 4x4s in off road difficult terrain. Ours was excellent but seemed in the minority. He had to stop 4 times to help other drivers who were literally stuck in the mud so lots of screeching burning tires and pumping diesel. The elephants didn't seem to mind however and we saw over 20 including lone males, babies and groups of females. Charming in the end despite some chaotic driving.
title: Chaotic but overall a good afternoon with the elephants

body: One could see herds of over 40 to 50 wild elephants at very close range, They did not seem to be dangerous in any way.
title: Good place to se Elephants

body: this park is very close to Habarana and is less visited than the more renown national parks that are nearby.This means smaller entrance fees and smaller jeep/guide fees and the biggest plus is less traffic in the park.We went for the birding and possible elephants and we saw plenty of both.It was a great 4 hour afternoon trip.We organized the trip through Habarana Inn and appears to be the cheapest in town as they own their own jeep which keeps the costs down.Knowledgeable guide.Highly recommend this trip
title: Lots of elephants

body: Had intended to go to Minneriya NP but was off season for elephants there [April] so was offered alternative trip to Hurulu Eco Park. Trip organised by company based at entrance to Chaaya Village/Cinnamon lodge. Jeep Ok , guide provided was sweet but spoke virtually no English and identified a number of birds incorrectly according to two bird books that I had so I didn't have much faith in his wildlife knowledge. We spent three hours in the park and saw a couple of elephants from a distance , with sightings shared between us and 5 other jeeps. A bit disappointing. Then, on way home from highway saw several large herds of elephants , some really close , apparently they like to hang out there and are more easily visible in clearings near the road. My teenagers enjoyed the jeep ride , and it might be worth considering if you are not going to a national park elsewhere e.g. Yala or Uda Walawe, otherwise save your money and just head to the highway !
title: Saw more elephants from the highway than in the eco park
Great Park to see wild elephants and birds
body: We were suspicious of this Park as it was recommended to us instead of Minneryia and due to the name Eco Park we thought it may be more like a zoo. I am glad we decided to go since we saw over 50 elephants and well over 30 water buffalo including a new born struggling to stand for first time. Plenty of birds as well including eagles, hawks. Thus, it was a great safari and our two kids (who had never been on safari before) loved it. It really depends on the time of year as to whether you should go to this Park, Minneryia, or Kaudulla but I am happy everyone including our driver steered us into the right Park. Not disappointed. If you want to see some other wild animals than described above you should go to those bigger National Parks and try your luck, though in wet season you are not likely to see much plus parks like Minneryia get flooded and is unaccessible and also is more expensive. Btw - great time to visit is late afternoon like 3pm onwards so you can be in the park during sunset

title: Good for elephants
body: We hadn't planned to go to this national park but it was recommended by our driver because of the high number of elephants and we weren't dissapointed. Saw loads of birds as well.

title: Disappointing
body: Perhaps it was the wrong time or the wrong season, but this was a wildlife park without wildlife. In an hour of bumpy driving, we saw one single disgruntled elephant enveloped in diesel fumes and surrounded by a dozen (literally) tourist jeeps, their drivers jockeying for position.I am so glad we saw Yalla a few years ago so we know that not all Sri Lankan wildlife parks are like this. At Yalla we saw 25 different species. Here we saw one elephant!

title: An element of luck needed here!
body: The local elephant population moves between the three parks according to their water and food needs. During our visit they were in the Eco Park.You need a good guide who will hopefully keep you clear of the parade of tourist jeeps. We didn't see that many elephants but there were plenty of birds to make up for that.AT the park entrance a ranger will try and get in your jeep. If you have a knowledgeable guide it really isn't necessary to pay for a ranger.

title: ELEPHANT SAFARI
body: Wonderful elephant safari. The only animals to see in this park though we did see an eagle

title: Great place to see elephants
body: This is a good place to see elephants especially during the off season (when access to the Minneriya and Kaudulla National Parks is difficult when the tanks are totally filled with water)But hardly any birds to be seen unlike in the case of Minneriya and Kaudulla National parks (no tanks / lakes)

title: Elephants Galore
body: This is an easily accessible, relatively small national park in North-Central Sri Lanka, very close to Sigiriya. It is very easy to fit climibing Sigiriya in the morning and an evening/sunset safari of the Hurulu Ecopark in the same day.Elelphants are the main attraction here, though we saw other wildlife such as, wild water buffolo, eagles and other bird life. Didn't see any peacocks and deer, though these specicies are considered relatively abundant in the park. Our guide/driver pointed out that the deer were there but not visible due to the tall grass, which was unusually tall due to some heavy rain the park had received preceeding our visit. Observed peacocks, just outside the park.Must have seen over 50 elephants in four separate herds, including new borns (possibly less than 3 months old). The guides and drivers are well trained and respect the distance rules from the elephants. The Forest Department does a very good job of maintaining the park well (of course the tracks are rugged but usable) and advising the guides of the areas within the park where the elephants are likely to be. Only downside was there were too many safari groups in the park. We were told that the number was particularlu high at the time mainly due to two other adjacent parks (Minneriya and one other) being closed to visitors due to flooding, forcing all tour operators to use Hurulu park. Hopefully, this will not be the case, when all three parks are open.Hurulu Ecopark would have to rank very high on the list of wildlife parks where one can observe the Asian elephant in the wild . For what we paid (around A$50, for a family of four), very few widlife experiences anywhere else in the world would be able to even come close in the value-for-money stakes.Highly recommend a half day (evening/sunset) safari of Hurulu Park to any Sri Lankan or a visitor to Sri Lanka.

title: Just Magical.
body: This had to be the highlight of our visit to Sri Lanka. Large forest area teeming with wildlife. If I were to recommend just one excursion whilst visiting Sri Lanka this is it.Still relatively unknown, so not packed with other visitors. In fact we didn't see anyone else until we were leaving the park. I think the photos to go with this tell the story. Don't miss it !!
